lens.name: silent-failures
lens.focus: Error handling and fallbacks. List every catch, .catch, default-on-error, optional chaining or ?? fallback, retry, timeout and early return that the change adds or touches. For each, ask: which unexpected errors could it hide; did the request or spec ask for this fallback; should the failure propagate or fail closed instead; is a retry limited to transient failures, bounded by one deadline, and does it keep the original failure and its classification; does every pending or in-flight state end on every path. A failed security, isolation or inspection check that ends in silent success or an unchecked path is a blocker.

lens.name: test-gaps
lens.focus: Tests. For each new or changed behaviour, find the test that would fail if that behaviour regressed, and say so when none exists. Flag tests that assert the defect they should catch, compare the code with itself, mock away the logic under test, pass for the wrong reason (invalid fixture, swallowed error, early return, wrong file), or were weakened, skipped or special-cased to pass. Name the missing or broken test case precisely. A test gap that hides a real defect in the change is at least major; report the underlying defect itself as its own finding.

lens.name: trust-boundaries
lens.focus: Secrets, untrusted input and isolation. Trace every credential, token, private value and untrusted input (issue or PR text, gate or test output, model output, configuration or scripts from the change) from its source to every sink: logs, events, errors, PR comments, commit metadata, branch names, model prompts, files and network. Check that redaction happens after decoding and before truncation, on error and retry paths as well as the normal one. Check sandbox profiles, deny lists and allowlists for path aliases, symlinks, files versus directories, environment variables and child processes. Anything that steers the factory must come from the base commit, never the change. When isolation or a check cannot be confirmed, the code must refuse with a clear reason, never fall back silently.

findings.title: An excluded queued trial aborts the entire evaluation
findings.detail: `toTarget` now throws for an excluded model, but this call occurs before the trial's error handler. If a queued trial's model becomes excluded before the trial starts, the exception escapes the worker and fails the whole eval, interrupting unrelated queued or running trials instead of recording the affected trial's failure.
findings.suggestion: Handle the origin exclusion inside the trial's error boundary and record the affected trial with the exclusion reason, allowing unrelated trials to continue.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval contains several models or cases; while one trial is waiting behind another, its runtime model is patched from US to CN under a CN exclusion. When that trial starts, the eval fails and remaining trials are interrupted.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:617 calls `let target = router.toTarget(model, effort ?? null);` before the trial-level `try` at line 625. src/router/router.ts:168 throws on exclusion: `if (origin) throw new Error(`${m.id}: ${origin}`);`. The worker catches this at src/evals/runner.ts:501–502 with `failed = true; throw error;`, and the run handler at line 524 calls `store.interruptEval(run.id, (error as Error).message, "failed")`. src/db/store.ts:554–557 marks remaining queued/running trials `skipped`.
verification.trigger: With CN excluded, patch a runtime model from US to CN while its trial waits behind another trial. When the queued trial starts, target construction throws outside its error handler, failing the eval and skipping remaining queued trials in that provider group.

findings.title: Verifier failure can omit the exclusion that exhausted the choices
findings.detail: The exclusion reason is propagated only when every listed verifier is excluded. If an allowed verifier remains but is ineligible because it raised the candidate, `pickVerifier` throws a different error that omits the excluded alternative. The invocation therefore fails without the required origin exclusion reason.
findings.suggestion: Include collected exclusion reasons when verifier selection fails after filtering, and log excluded verifier choices.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier list contains an allowed model that raised the candidate and a CN model excluded by configuration. No verifier can be selected, but the error reports only that the allowed model raised the candidate.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1347 only reports exclusions when `!listed.length && exclusions.length`; line 1349 otherwise calls `pickVerifier(listed, avoidVendors, avoidModels, identity)`. src/pipeline/review.ts:325–327 throws `NoCapacityError(`verifier ${targets.map((t) => t.modelId).join(", ")} raised a candidate it would check`)` when no independent model remains, without the collected exclusions.
verification.trigger: With CN excluded, configure verifier targets containing one CN model and one allowed model that raised the candidate. The allowed model keeps `listed` nonempty, but independence selection fails; the error omits the origin exclusion reason explicitly required for exhaustion.

findings.title: Skip native smoke checks when all of a provider’s models are excluded
findings.detail: Native checks still run when a configured exclusion removes every model for Claude or Codex. `cheapestModel` throws the exclusion reason, which `runChecks` records as a failure; `reportChecks` then returns a nonzero exit code. This makes `limitless deploy --smoke` fail for an intentional configuration even if other eligible providers work. Backend checks already treat an entirely excluded provider as skipped.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same excluded-provider skip handling to native checks before selecting a model.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure an origin exclusion that excludes every Claude model while leaving another provider eligible, then run the deployment smoke check. Every Claude check fails instead of being skipped, so deployment fails.

verification.evidence: scripts/smoke.ts:1019–1020 selects `cheapestModel(id, catalog.models, excludeOrigins)` for native checks without an exclusion skip guard. scripts/smoke.ts:353–354 throws when `models.length && !eligible.length`. scripts/smoke.ts:157–159 converts that exception to `fail(String(error), ...)`, and scripts/smoke.ts:341 returns exit code 1 whenever `rows.some((row) => row.status === "fail")`.
verification.trigger: Keep Claude enabled and configure exclusions covering every Claude model, while another provider remains eligible. All seven Claude smoke checks fail with the exclusion reason instead of skipping, causing deployment with smoke checks to fail.

findings.title: Draft deferrals never resume when GitHub polling is disabled
findings.detail: Skipped draft triggers are no longer returned by pendingConflictTriggers, and the only code that reactivates them is in the GitHub poller. The supported github.poll = false configuration does not start that poller, so a land-triggered conflict deferred while a PR is a draft remains skipped permanently, even after the PR becomes ready or the daemon restarts.
findings.suggestion: Provide a change-observation path for installations with polling disabled, or preserve a bounded fallback for that configuration.
findings.failure_scenario: Set github.poll = false, create a land conflict trigger while the PR is a draft, then mark the PR ready on the same head. Subsequent conflict processing never sees the skipped trigger and no round starts.

verification.evidence: src/db/store.ts:1114 selects only "WHERE state = 'pending'", excluding draft deferrals marked "state = 'skipped'" at src/db/store.ts:1190. src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:14 processes only "store.pendingConflictTriggers()". The sole reactivation call is "store.recheckDraftConflictTriggers(pr.url, snap)" at src/integrations/github-poller.ts:374; src/integrations/index.ts:38–45 disables that poller when githubPoll is false.
verification.trigger: With github.poll=false, a land conflict trigger is skipped because its PR is draft. Marking the PR ready on the same head never reactivates that trigger; subsequent conflict processing and daemon restarts leave it skipped, so no round starts.

candidates.title: A head change can be missed while a draft lookup is in flight
candidates.detail: The request says to recheck a draft deferral when the poller observes “a new head.” This guard compares the snapshot only with the poller's previous snapshot. If the poller saves the new head before an in-flight live lookup marks an older-head trigger as draft, subsequent polls see the same head and never call recheckDraftConflictTriggers, even though that method would detect the mismatch against the trigger's observed SHA. The deferred trigger remains stale until another qualifying change occurs.
candidates.suggestion: Check deferred triggers against each observed snapshot, or otherwise make recording the deferral and observing the head change race-safe.
candidates.failure_scenario: A trigger for head A starts a live lookup. While it is awaiting GitHub, the poller observes and saves draft head B. The lookup then returns a draft result and marks the A trigger skipped. Later polls continue to observe draft head B, so the skipped trigger is never rechecked for the A-to-B head change.

findings.title: A saved head change can be lost before the draft deferral is rechecked
findings.detail: The poller saves the new snapshot before reactivating draft triggers, and uses the saved snapshot on the next pass to decide whether the head changed. The same ordering can occur when a live lookup finishes after the poller has saved the newer head and marks the trigger as draft. The trigger remains skipped despite the poller having observed a new head.
findings.suggestion: Make recording the observation and reactivating eligible draft triggers durable together, or compare each deferred trigger's recorded head with the current observation on every poll.
findings.failure_scenario: A trigger is skipped as draft at head A. The poller observes draft head B and saves it, then the daemon restarts before rechecking triggers. Subsequent observations of draft head B do not reactivate the trigger.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land conflict
findings.detail: A land trigger is immediately evaluated against any saved poller snapshot, even if that snapshot predates the approved head. `startConflictTrigger` marks the trigger skipped when the saved head differs, and a later poll cannot reconsider it. The queue has already blocked the entry, so the requested conflict round never starts.
findings.suggestion: Refresh the PR observation before rejecting a land trigger for a stale head, or retain the trigger pending until a current observation can decide it.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller last observed head A; a review round pushes head B and B is approved before the next poll. Landing B conflicts with the base, but the saved snapshot still says A, so the B trigger is permanently skipped as `PR head moved`.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:16–21 reads the saved snapshot and calls `if (snapshot) store.startConflictTrigger(trigger.id, snapshot, now())`, bypassing a fresh lookup. src/db/store.ts:1126–1127 rejects `seen.headRefOid !== trigger.head` as `"PR head moved"`; lines 1137–1140 persist `state = 'skipped'`.
verification.trigger: Saved snapshot A plus a land trigger for approved head B permanently skips that land trigger. A later poller event may independently start a round.

findings.title: A conflict observed during another round is lost permanently
findings.detail: An active review or conflict round causes the trigger to be marked skipped. The poller emits `pr.conflicting` only on entry into the conflicting state, so if the active round fails or ends without changing the head, subsequent polls do not create another trigger. The unresolved conflict therefore never gets its own round.
findings.suggestion: Keep the trigger pending while another round is active and reconsider it when that round terminates, subject to a fresh PR observation and the daily cap.
findings.failure_scenario: A review round is in flight when the poller first observes the PR as CONFLICTING. The trigger is skipped; the review round later fails without pushing, and every subsequent poll still sees CONFLICTING, so no conflict round starts.

verification.evidence: src/db/store.ts:1130–1140 rejects any nonterminal round with `? "round in flight"` and permanently consumes the trigger via `UPDATE conflict_triggers SET state = 'skipped', reason = ? WHERE id = ?`. src/db/store.ts:1071 retries only `WHERE state = 'pending'`. src/integrations/github-poller.ts:206 emits another event only when `next.mergeable === "CONFLICTING" && prev?.mergeable !== "CONFLICTING"`; lines 367–374 save that observation before consuming its trigger.
verification.trigger: An open factory PR becomes CONFLICTING while a review round is active. Its conflict trigger becomes skipped. If the review round then fails without changing the head, continued CONFLICTING observations produce no new event, so no conflict round starts.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land trigger
findings.detail: The land path uses any stored GitHub snapshot without refreshing it. `startConflictTrigger` marks the trigger skipped when that snapshot's head differs from the land entry's approved head, even if the snapshot is simply older than the approval. The trigger is then no longer pending, so this landing-queue trigger cannot recover on restart.
findings.suggestion: Refresh or otherwise establish the snapshot's freshness before permanently skipping a land trigger; retain it pending when the observation cannot establish the current head.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller saved head A, the PR advances to B and B is approved before the next poll, and the land queue detects a conflict at B. Processing compares B with the saved A and skips the trigger instead of starting a round.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:21 uses the saved snapshot whenever present. src/db/store.ts:1126–1127 compares its head with the trigger head; lines 1137–1140 execute `UPDATE conflict_triggers SET state = 'skipped', reason = ? WHERE id = ?`. Pending processing selects only `state = 'pending'` (lines 1068–1072).
verification.trigger: Landing B conflicts while the saved snapshot still records A; the B land trigger is permanently skipped instead of starting a round.

findings.title: Retrying comment creation can post duplicate resolution comments
findings.detail: The `gh` wrapper retries transient failures around the entire comment command. If GitHub creates the comment but its response is lost, the retry creates another comment without checking the marker again. The preflight marker lookup only protects a later delivery attempt, not retries within this call.
findings.suggestion: Recheck for the marker after an uncertain comment outcome before issuing another creation request.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts `pr comment`, but the client receives a timeout or connection reset; the retry posts a second comment with the same conflict-round marker.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1894 checks for the marker once, then :1899 calls `await gh(["pr", "comment", prUrl, "--body-file", "-"], ctx.signal, text)`. At :1922, gh wraps each call in `withGitHubRetry(...)`. src/git/repos.ts:55 treats command timeouts as transient; :91–97 retries the same call without repeating the marker lookup.
verification.trigger: GitHub creates the comment but its acknowledgement times out while retry budget remains. Retrying comment creation posts another identical resolution comment, violating the one-comment requirement.

findings.title: Auto-merge is disabled before validating the PR delivery grant
findings.detail: The new auto-merge mutation occurs before `stored()` and `assertFactoryBranchPush` verify that the PR is still open, belongs to the expected branch and repository, and matches the round's current grant. A stale or invalid round can therefore modify the PR even though delivery is subsequently refused.
findings.suggestion: Validate the current grant and PR identity before disabling auto-merge, and revalidate after the mutation before pushing.
findings.failure_scenario: The PR head branch changes while a conflict round runs and auto-merge is enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge, then rejects the changed branch.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1865–1866 executes `if (review.kind === "conflict" && pr.autoMerge) await gh(["pr", "merge", prUrl, "--disable-auto"], ctx.signal)`. Only afterward, :1869–1870 calls `stored()` and `assertFactoryBranchPush(...)`. src/core/delivery.ts:88 rejects a changed branch: `if (pr.headBranch !== branch) return ...`.
verification.trigger: The PR head branch changes during the round and auto-merge is enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge on that PR before rejecting the changed branch.

findings.title: Restart tests do not cover a stale saved observation
findings.detail: The restart tests use either no saved observation or one matching the trigger. They therefore pass while a saved observation for an older head causes a durable land trigger to be skipped permanently, and while an outdated open, non-draft observation can start an ineligible round.
findings.suggestion: Add restart and land-trigger cases with an older saved head and with a PR that became draft or closed after the saved observation. Assert that a current observation governs whether the trigger starts.
findings.failure_scenario: A pending trigger for head B is recovered while the database still contains an open CONFLICTING snapshot for head A; the existing tests never exercise this state.

verification.evidence: test/conflict-rounds.test.ts:330–340 records a trigger and reopens the database without saving an observation. The other startup test uses the same head for both: :517 `recordConflictTrigger(url, await remoteHead(), ...)` and :525 `headRefOid: await remoteHead()`. Neither covers differing heads. src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:21 consumes any saved snapshot; src/db/store.ts:1126–1127 checks `seen.headRefOid !== trigger.head`, then :1139 permanently sets the trigger to `state = 'skipped'`.
verification.trigger: Recover a pending trigger for head B with a saved OPEN/CONFLICTING observation for head A. Recovery skips the trigger; both existing restart tests pass without exercising this state.

findings.title: The non-factory polling case bypasses the poller
findings.detail: The non-factory branch inserts a trigger and calls the store consumer directly, so it does not test whether polling a non-factory PR creates a round. A regression in tracking, event generation, or poller consumption for that case would still pass the test.
findings.suggestion: Exercise a tracked non-factory PR through the same fake GitHub poller path as the other eligibility cases and assert that no conflict round starts.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller erroneously starts a conflict round for a non-factory PR, but the test bypasses the poller and continues to pass.

verification.evidence: test/conflict-rounds.test.ts:365–371 handles `eligibility === "non-factory"` by directly calling `recordConflictTrigger(...)` and `startConflictTrigger(...)`. The `startGitHubPoller(...)` call at :373 is exclusively in the `else` branch. The zero-round assertion at :393 therefore verifies only the direct consumer for this case.
verification.trigger: A regression in polling behavior for non-factory PRs would not be exercised by the non-factory test case, which bypasses the poller and could continue passing.

findings.title: Persisted conflict filenames bypass credential redaction
findings.detail: Conflict paths come from the repository under review and are copied into run state without credential redaction. The state is subsequently persisted by updateRun, so a registered credential embedded in a filename reaches storage even though the later PR comment redacts it.
findings.suggestion: Redact credential-bearing paths before storing them or sending them to any external sink, while retaining whatever representation is needed for local conflict resolution.
findings.failure_scenario: A changed repository contains a conflicting filename that includes a registered token; the token is stored in conflictFiles in the run state.

verification.evidence: src/git/merge.ts:79–83 obtains conflict paths from git stdout and returns them. src/pipeline/engine.ts:2245 assigns `ctx.state.conflictFiles = conflicts`; :2252 persists that state through `ctx.store.updateRun(..., ctx.state)`. src/db/store.ts:1485–1486 stores `json(state)`, and :71–72 defines json using plain `JSON.stringify(v)` without redaction.
verification.trigger: A conflicting filename contains a registered credential of sufficient length for substring redaction. The raw filename is serialized into persisted conflictFiles without credential redaction.

findings.title: Disable auto-merge only after validating the delivery grant and PR head
findings.detail: The new GitHub mutation runs before stored() and assertFactoryBranchPush validate that the grant still holds and that the PR is still open on the expected branch and head. A stale conflict round can therefore change auto-merge settings even when its delivery is subsequently refused.
findings.suggestion: Validate the current grant and PR identity before disabling auto-merge, and recheck state after the mutation before pushing.
findings.failure_scenario: The PR head or round grant changes while a conflict round is running and auto-merge is enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge, then rejects the stale round.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1865–1866 disables auto-merge before :1869 invokes `stored()` and :1870 invokes `assertFactoryBranchPush(...)`. The stored-record change guard at :1851–1857 throws `the round's record changed during delivery`; src/core/delivery.ts:77–80 rejects mismatched remote or PR head SHAs.
verification.trigger: The PR head moves, or the stored round grant changes after initial validation, while auto-merge is enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge before rejecting the stale round.

findings.title: An untrusted PR comment can suppress the resolution comment
findings.detail: The idempotency check accepts the marker in any PR comment without verifying its author. A PR participant can post the predictable marker before delivery, causing the factory to treat the required resolution summary as already published.
findings.suggestion: Tie the checkpoint to a trusted factory-authored comment or another durable publication record rather than trusting arbitrary comment text.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR participant posts `<!-- limitless-conflict-round:<run-id> -->` before the round delivers; the merge is pushed but no factory resolution summary is posted.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1889 marks the round delivered before :1892 fetches PR comments. At :1894, `if (!comments?.some((comment) => comment.body?.includes(marker)))` controls whether the summary is posted. The inspected comment structure at :1893 contains only `body`; no author or factory ownership check is performed.
verification.trigger: A PR participant posts a comment containing the round's marker before delivery. After pushing the merge, the factory treats that comment as its own and skips the required resolution summary.

findings.detail: When a saved poller snapshot exists, trigger processing uses it without refreshing the PR. A PR can become draft or close without changing its head, so the saved observation still passes the start checks. Delivery eventually checks draft status, but the forbidden round and its model work have already started.
findings.suggestion: Refresh the PR state before starting a pending conflict trigger, and leave the trigger pending if its current state cannot be verified.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller saves an open non-draft PR, the owner converts it to draft, and a land conflict trigger is processed before the next poll. A conflict round starts from the stale snapshot.

verification.trigger: A saved non-draft snapshot remains after the owner converts the PR to draft. A matching-head land trigger creates a conflict round despite the draft exclusion; the later delivery guard does not prevent that work from starting.

The later poll updates the snapshot, but the skipped trigger is never reconsidered, so the blocked entry has no round.
findings.suggestion: Refresh the PR observation for a land trigger, or leave a trigger pending when its saved observation is older than the trigger head and retry after a fresh observation.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller last observed head A, the PR advances to B and B is approved before the next poll, then the land queue detects a conflict at B. The saved A snapshot causes the only land trigger to be skipped permanently.

candidates.title: Persisted conflict filenames bypass credential redaction
candidates.detail: Conflict paths come from the repository under review and are copied into run state without credential redaction. The state is subsequently persisted by updateRun, so a registered credential embedded in a filename reaches storage even though the later PR comment redacts it.

candidates.title: Disable auto-merge only after validating the delivery grant and PR head

candidates.title: An untrusted PR comment can suppress the resolution comment

candidates.title: Auto-merge is disabled before verifying the PR and delivery grant
candidates.detail: The new conflict delivery path changes GitHub state before assertFactoryBranchPush validates that the PR is open, still has the authorized head and branch, and still belongs to the expected repository. If polling is disabled or does not produce another observation for the PR, a transient `gh` failure leaves the conflict unresolved indefinitely until a restart or unrelated block.

candidates.detail: A poller trigger is permanently skipped unless the owning run has already reached succeeded or needs_human. A factory PR can be open and tracked while its owning run is still finishing delivery. Once skipped, the poller will not emit another pr.conflicting event while mergeability remains CONFLICTING.
candidates.suggestion: Keep the trigger pending while the owning run is still delivering, and reconsider it when that run reaches a terminal state.
candidates.failure_scenario: The poller observes a newly opened factory PR as CONFLICTING while its owner is still running. The trigger is marked skipped as not a factory PR; the owner subsequently succeeds, but subsequent polls see the same conflicting state and never start a round.

candidates.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land conflict trigger
candidates.detail: The request says a landing-queue entry blocked by a conflict starts a conflict round and that the trigger survives restart. If any saved PR snapshot exists, processing uses it without refreshing it. When that snapshot has an older head than the land entry's approved head, startConflictTrigger marks the trigger skipped as "PR head moved". It is then no longer pending, so a later poll of the correct head cannot recover it.
candidates.suggestion: Refresh the PR observation before deciding eligibility for a land trigger, or retain the trigger pending until a current observation can be checked.
candidates.failure_scenario: The poller last observed head A, the PR advances to B and B is approved for landing before the next poll, and the land queue finds a base conflict. The trigger records B but is permanently skipped against the saved snapshot of A.

duplicates.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land trigger
duplicates.detail: When any saved snapshot exists, the trigger is processed against it without a fresh PR lookup. If the snapshot predates the land entry's approved head, `startConflictTrigger` marks the trigger skipped as `PR head moved`. A later poll cannot recover it because the trigger is no longer pending, and a conflicting mergeability episode may already have been observed.
duplicates.suggestion: Obtain a current observation before deciding eligibility for a land trigger, or leave mismatched observations pending until a current observation resolves them.
duplicates.failure_scenario: The poller last saved head A, the PR advances to head B, and the land queue approves B and finds a conflict before the next poll. The trigger for B is permanently skipped against snapshot A.

candidates.title: Failed trigger lookups are not retried during normal operation
candidates.detail: A lookup error leaves the trigger pending, but this catch only logs the error. The queue processes pending triggers only at startup or after another land entry blocks. If polling is disabled or does not produce another observation for the PR, a transient `gh` failure leaves the conflict unresolved indefinitely until a restart or unrelated block.
candidates.suggestion: Arrange a bounded, durable retry for pending lookups during normal operation, without depending on another land failure or daemon restart.
candidates.failure_scenario: A land conflict is recorded while `gh pr view` temporarily fails and there is no saved PR snapshot. The command later recovers, but no further land conflict or PR poll occurs, so the pending trigger never starts.

candidates.title: A stale saved PR observation can start or discard a land trigger
candidates.detail: When any saved GitHub snapshot exists, the trigger consumer uses it without checking the current PR. A snapshot from before the land conflict can say the PR is draft or has a different head, causing the durable trigger to be permanently skipped; it can also say the PR is open and ready after it has become draft or closed, starting a round that should not start. Poller startup likewise consumes pending triggers from the saved snapshot before polling. The restart test supplies a current snapshot and therefore does not cover this case.
candidates.suggestion: Verify land and resumed triggers against a current PR observation before consuming them, and test stale snapshots against changed draft, state and head values.
candidates.failure_scenario: The last poll recorded head A; the PR advances to head B and the landing queue detects a conflict at B before the next poll. Processing compares B to the saved A and marks the only land trigger skipped, so no conflict round starts from that trigger.

candidates.title: The non-factory poller case bypasses the poller
candidates.detail: The non-factory branch manually inserts and consumes a trigger instead of running the poller. It verifies the store's refusal but cannot catch a regression in how polling handles a conflicting non-factory PR, despite the test name and the requested poller acceptance case.
candidates.suggestion: Drive a non-factory conflicting PR through the fake GitHub poller and assert that it starts no round.
candidates.failure_scenario: A future change makes the poller start rounds for non-factory observations while the direct store-level setup in this test still passes.

candidates.title: Missing draft state is treated as permission to proceed
candidates.detail: The PR lookup converts a missing or invalid `isDraft` field to false. Conflict delivery therefore proceeds when GitHub's response does not establish that the PR is ready for review. The poller admission path likewise treats an absent `isDraft` as false. This fails open at a condition the request explicitly requires.
candidates.suggestion: Require a boolean draft state in both the direct lookup and poller snapshot before starting or delivering a conflict round; refuse or leave the trigger pending when it cannot be confirmed.
candidates.failure_scenario: A PR lookup or stored snapshot omits `isDraft` for a draft PR. The conflict round is admitted and the delivery check sees `false`, allowing a push to the draft branch.

candidates.title: Auto-merge is disabled before validating the current PR head
candidates.detail: The new delivery path changes the PR's auto-merge setting before checking that the PR is still open, belongs to the expected repository and branch, and remains at the reviewed head. A stale round can therefore mutate a PR even though the subsequent delivery guard rejects it.
candidates.suggestion: Validate the stored grant and current PR identity before disabling auto-merge, then revalidate after the awaited mutation and before pushing.
candidates.failure_scenario: The PR head changes while a conflict round runs and a user enables auto-merge for the new head. The stale round disables auto-merge, then fails its head check without pushing.

candidates.title: The PR comment does not summarize the resolution
candidates.detail: The request requires that "The PR gets one comment summarizing the resolution." The comment reports the base SHA and conflicted file names, but contains no account of how the conflicting changes were reconciled. A reader cannot assess the resolution from it.
candidates.suggestion: Include a concise, reviewed summary of the actual resolution in the comment, with the existing publication and redaction checks.
candidates.failure_scenario: A conflict in a file is resolved by combining two behavioral changes; the resulting comment names the file and commit but does not explain the combined behavior.

findings.title: Cached first attempts lose the workspace needed by retries after restart
findings.detail: A completed first attempt is reused from state after restart, but the resumed stage cleans the checkout before reaching this line. A pending or newly started retry therefore runs without the build output or other files produced by that first attempt. Previously, a resumed gate stage reran the first attempt and recreated those files before retrying.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the workspace required by a pending retry, or replay the local first attempt before performing the retry after restart.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate setup creates an ignored build directory, a check fails transiently, and the daemon restarts before or during its retry. On resume, checkoutCommitted removes the directory, the cached initial result is reused, and the retry fails because its build output is missing.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1157 calls `await checkoutCommitted(cwd, ...)` before the initial execution. src/git/repos.ts:476 runs `git clean -ffdxq`, removing ignored build output. src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:23 returns `results[purpose]` without running setup; src/gates/run.ts:280 retries with `{ ...cfg, setup: [], checks: selected }`.
verification.trigger: Restart after the initial failure is checkpointed but before its regression retry completes. Resume removes setup-generated files, reuses the initial result, and retries without rebuilding those files, causing a false failure.

findings.title: Executor events are never consumed
findings.detail: The shared execution path awaits only `result` and never reads `execution.events`. Gate reporting and landing logs currently work only because the local executor calls hooks directly; an executor implementing the advertised interface has no way to deliver its streamed check events to those consumers.
findings.suggestion: Consume the event stream in the shared execution path and forward events to the appropriate gate and landing reporting hooks, coordinating stream completion and errors with the result.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor yields check events and returns a valid GateRun. The stage verdict is computed, but no per-check pipeline events or landing check output are recorded.

verification.evidence: src/gates/executor.ts:139 attaches the execution, then :147 only does `return await execution.result`; nothing consumes `execution.events`. Hooks are invoked directly only by the local implementation at :87: `hooks.onResult?.(r, phase)`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:357 records per-check events through `onResult`; src/land/queue.ts:397-398 likewise writes check output through that hook.
verification.trigger: Inject an executor that supplies check events through its events iterable and returns a GateRun. Verdict calculation succeeds, but ordinary per-check pipeline events and landing check output are missing.

findings.title: Restarting a retry removes the first attempt's build output
findings.detail: A resumed gates stage cleans the checkout before retrieving its saved initial result and attaching to the pending retry. The retry therefore runs without files created by the initial attempt, despite the existing requirement that retries see the same build output. Prepare likewise discards changes before resuming its baseline retry.
findings.suggestion: Preserve or reconstruct the first attempt's required workspace state before resuming a local retry, with restart coverage for checks that depend on generated files.
findings.failure_scenario: A setup or initial check creates an untracked build artifact, a later check fails transiently, and the daemon restarts during its retry. The resumed retry cannot find the artifact and produces a different verdict.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1157 unconditionally calls `await checkoutCommitted(cwd, undefined, Boolean(ctx.state.implementerIssue));` before resuming gates. src/git/repos.ts:476 executes `["git", "clean", "-ffdxq"]`, deleting untracked and ignored build output. src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:23 returns cached initial results via `if (results[purpose]) return results[purpose];`, so setup and successful initial checks do not recreate that output. src/gates/run.ts:280 resumes retries with `await runner({ ...cfg, setup: [], checks: selected });`.
verification.trigger: Setup or a successful initial check creates an untracked artifact needed by a later, transiently failing check. The daemon restarts during the regression retry. Resume deletes the artifact, skips the cached initial execution, and reruns only the failed check without setup, potentially turning a passing retry into a blocking failure.

findings.title: A checkpoint failure leaves started work uncancelled
findings.detail: The executor starts work before persisting its handle, but if persistence rejects, execution exits without attaching or cancelling. An executor whose start actually launches work can continue indefinitely without a durable handle, and a subsequent attempt can start duplicate work.
findings.suggestion: On persistence failure, attach to the returned handle and cancel the execution before propagating the failure, while preserving the original error.
findings.failure_scenario: A remote executor starts a gate suite and the state save fails because the database write fails; the run fails while the untracked suite continues.

verification.evidence: src/gates/executor.ts:137-139 executes `await executor.start(req, signal)`, then `await persist(handle)`, then `executor.attach(handle, signal)`. Cancellation is registered only afterwards at :141-144. src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:46 persists with `await ctx.save("gate-started")`; its catch at :54-56 rethrows without cancelling.
verification.trigger: An injected executor starts external work and persistence rejects. executeGate exits before attaching or registering cancellation, leaving that work uncancelled by this path. This requires an executor beyond the shipped local implementation, whose start only allocates a handle.

findings.title: Redacting the local handle changes the request replayed after restart
findings.detail: The local handle contains the gate request, including commands and paths, but the persisted copy is transformed by `redactGateData`. On restart, local attach executes that transformed request rather than the trusted gate configuration. Credential redaction or terminal-control stripping can change a valid command or path, so the resumed run can check different behavior or fail unexpectedly.
findings.suggestion: Keep sensitive request data out of the persisted handle and reconstruct the local request from trusted run state when reattaching, without transforming executable input.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured gate command contains a registered credential or a terminal control character; after a restart, the local executor runs the redacted or stripped command.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:44 persists `handle: redactGateData(handle)`. src/gates/output.ts:23 applies `redactCredentials(stripVTControlCharacters(output))` to strings. src/gates/executor.ts:60 reads `const req = handle.request` and :77–81 executes `req.gates`; :137 prefers the stored handle over the current request.
verification.trigger: A pending local command contains a registered credential substring or terminal formatting sequence. After restart, attachment executes the sanitized command instead of the original, potentially changing its result.

findings.title: Executor event streams are never consumed
findings.detail: The shared execution path awaits only the result and never reads `execution.events`. The local executor invokes hooks directly, masking the issue, but an injected executor that reports progress and check results through the interface loses those events; landing logs and pipeline gate events are absent.
findings.suggestion: Consume the event stream while awaiting the result and route events to the appropriate hooks, propagating stream failures according to the executor contract.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor yields check events and returns a GateRun without invoking local hooks. The gate completes but its check events and landing log output are silently missing.

verification.evidence: src/gates/executor.ts:147 awaits only `execution.result`, never the `events` iterable declared at :19. Local hooks are invoked separately at :87. src/land/queue.ts:397-398 appends check output only through `onResult`.
verification.trigger: An injected executor emits events without calling local hooks. Its GateRun completes, but per-check pipeline events and landing log output are omitted.

findings.title: Persisting a sanitized local request can change the command replayed after restart
findings.detail: The local handle contains the complete request, but redactGateData transforms every string before the handle is stored. A restart attaches using that transformed request, so a gate command or working directory containing a registered credential or terminal control character can differ from the original. The initial attachment uses the unsanitized handle, making behavior depend on whether the daemon restarted.
findings.suggestion: Persist a replayable request without storing secrets, for example by reconstructing the local request from trusted run state on resume, and keep redaction at the storage boundary.
findings.failure_scenario: A base gate command contains a string registered for credential redaction. The daemon stops after saving the handle; on resume, local attachment executes the command with that string replaced by the redaction marker.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:44 saves `handle: redactGateData(handle)`. src/gates/output.ts:31 sanitizes every string; src/util/proc.ts:669 replaces matching credentials with `[redacted]`. src/gates/executor.ts:60 and :77–81 replay gates from `handle.request`.
verification.trigger: A base gate command contains a registered credential value and the daemon restarts after handle persistence. The resumed execution runs the command containing `[redacted]`, changing its semantics.

findings.title: Restart tests do not exercise replay of a persisted local request
findings.detail: The restart cases use a fake LAN executor whose handle has no request, while the local replay test serializes a handle directly without passing it through the persistence redaction path. Consequently they cannot catch a local request being changed before restart.
findings.suggestion: Add a restart test using the local executor and a request containing a value transformed by redaction, then verify the resumed check executes the original command.
findings.failure_scenario: A persisted local handle has a gate command altered by redaction; all current restart and local-attachment tests still pass.

verification.evidence: test/gate-executor.test.ts:159–162 resumes with `fake(...)` and `gateExecutor: fresh.executor`, recovering requests from `scripted.requests`. The local test at :223–226 uses `localExecutor().start(...)` then `executor.attach(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(handle)), signal)`, bypassing persistence. Actual persistence uses `handle: redactGateData(handle)` (src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:44); that function transforms every string (src/gates/output.ts:30–31).
verification.trigger: A local request's command changes during persistence redaction, then a restart replays the altered request. Neither the fake restart tests nor the direct local serialization test exercises that path, so this regression goes undetected.

findings.title: Legacy resume test cannot distinguish local selection from injected selection
findings.detail: The legacy-state test resumes with no injected executor, so local is the only available choice. It does not test the stated compatibility rule when another executor is selected. The selection code uses the injected executor whenever there is no stored handle.
findings.suggestion: Resume a pre-change run with a non-local fake executor configured and assert that the legacy gate runs locally without starting the fake.
findings.failure_scenario: A run created before handles existed resumes with a non-local executor injected and starts that executor instead of local; the current test still passes.

verification.evidence: The legacy test resumes with `const resumed = start(handler)` (test/gate-executor.test.ts:213), supplying no competing executor. Selection uses `stored?.kind === "local" ... ? localExecutor(hooks) : (injected ?? localExecutor(hooks))` (src/gates/executor.ts:132–135), then `stored ?? (await executor.start(req, signal))` (:137).
verification.trigger: Resume a legacy run with no stored handle and a non-local executor injected: selection starts the injected executor. The current test supplies no injection and therefore passes without distinguishing these behaviors.

findings.title: Redacting the local handle changes the command replayed after restart
findings.detail: The local handle embeds the gate request, including its working directory and base-configured commands. Redacting the entire handle before persistence changes any command or path containing a registered credential and strips terminal control sequences. On restart, `localExecutor.attach` executes that altered request rather than the original trusted gate configuration. A resumed gate can therefore test different conditions and report a pass for a check that would have failed.
findings.suggestion: Persist only the local execution identity and reconstruct its request from the trusted base configuration and current run context on resume, or otherwise preserve execution semantics without storing secret-bearing values.
findings.failure_scenario: A base gate command compares a value against a registered credential. The daemon restarts while that gate is pending; the persisted command contains the redaction marker instead of the original value, so the replay evaluates a different condition and can pass incorrectly.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:44 stores a redacted handle. src/util/proc.ts:669 performs `text.split(secret).join("[redacted]")`. src/gates/executor.ts:137–139 attaches the stored handle, and :60–81 executes its embedded request rather than the freshly supplied gate configuration.
verification.trigger: A pending command compares distinct literals that contain registered credential values. Redaction can make those literals equal; after restart the replay can pass a condition that originally failed.

findings.title: Resumed retries reuse results after their build output has been removed
findings.detail: The request says regression retries and baseline retries do not change, and the surrounding code requires retries to see the first attempt's build output. After a restart during a retry, this returns the saved initial result without rerunning the initial gate, while prepare has already called discardChanges and the gates stage has called checkoutCommitted. A local retry therefore runs in a cleaned checkout without the files produced by its initial attempt, potentially changing a pass into a failure or vice versa.
findings.suggestion: Restore the first attempt's required workspace state on local resume, or rerun the initial local execution before retrying while preserving the stored handle semantics for executors that can reattach.
findings.failure_scenario: A setup command generates an untracked build artifact, an initial check fails transiently, and the daemon restarts during its retry. On resume the artifact is cleaned, the saved initial result is reused, and the retry fails because the artifact is missing.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1157 cleans the checkout on stage entry; src/git/repos.ts:476 uses `git clean -ffdxq`. src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:23 immediately returns cached attempts. src/gates/run.ts:280 launches regression retries with `setup: []`.
verification.trigger: Restart during a regression retry whose initial setup generated an untracked artifact. Resume deletes the artifact, skips the cached initial execution, and reruns only the check, producing a false failure because the artifact is missing.

findings.title: Landing checks discard the execution handle
findings.detail: The request requires that the caller persist the handle before awaiting the execution and that landing queue checks use the executor. This call supplies neither a stored handle nor a persistence callback, so executeGate uses its no-op default. A restart during landing checks starts another execution instead of attaching to the existing one, leaving remote work duplicated and its result unobserved.
findings.suggestion: Persist the landing execution handle in durable queue state before attaching, and restore it when resuming the checks.
findings.failure_scenario: A landing check is running on an executor whose work survives daemon restart. The daemon restarts before the result arrives; the queue starts a second execution because the first handle was never stored.

(await executor.start(req, signal))`. src/land/queue.ts:297 explicitly states: '`checking` re-runs the checks from the start, like a `queued` entry.'

findings.title: Executor events are never consumed
findings.detail: The requested Execution exposes events and the local executor is to preserve gate events. executeGate awaits only result and never reads execution.events; existing progress and landing logs work only because the local implementation calls injected hooks directly. Any executor implementing the advertised interface emits events that are silently discarded, and landing logs contain no command output.
findings.suggestion: Consume the execution event stream in the shared path and translate its events into the existing hooks, including setup and status events as needed.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor emits check results through its events iterable while its result is pending. The pipeline displays no check progress, and landing writes only the log header despite the executor providing output.

verification.trigger: An injected executor emits check events while its result remains pending. No check progress is recorded; after completion, the landing log still contains only its header because the event stream never reaches the output hook.

findings.title: Resume discards handles for in-flight retries
findings.detail: Stored handles are reused only for baseline, initial, and rebase executions. A pending timeout, baseline retry, or regression retry is discarded when the stage resumes, and the executor starts replacement work instead of attaching to the existing execution. Cancellation cannot recover work owned by a previous daemon process. The new test explicitly expects this behavior, but it contradicts the requested restart contract.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough attempt context to resume each retry and attach to its recorded handle without starting it again.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after a remote regression retry starts but before its result is recorded. On resume, the retry handle is discarded and another execution is started while the original may still be running.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:24-32 requires `pending.purpose === purpose` and `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)`; otherwise it clears `ctx.state.gateExecution`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1156 resumes with purpose `"initial"` before reaching `"regression-retry"` at line 1195. src/gates/executor.ts:40 cancels only executions present in the process-local `liveExecutions` map.
verification.trigger: Restart with a persisted regression-retry handle. Resume discards it and starts initial gates again; a remote execution surviving the restart is neither attached nor cancelled. This violates the requested restart contract.

findings.title: Handle is cleared before the result has a durable checkpoint
findings.detail: The execution handle is removed and saved as soon as executeGate settles, before the caller records the gate result or the stage completion. A restart in that interval loses both the handle and the result, so the resumed stage starts the execution again. This also affects the initial execution, which otherwise has an attach path.
findings.suggestion: Keep the handle until the corresponding result or completed stage is durably saved, and resume by attaching when that checkpoint is absent.
findings.failure_scenario: A daemon stops immediately after the gate-result save but before the gates stage saves its comparison. Restarting the run starts a new execution instead of attaching to the completed one.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:59-64 returns the result through a finally block that executes `ctx.state.gateExecution = undefined; await ctx.save("gate-result")`. The result itself is not saved there. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1189 computes the comparison later, and line 1219 assigns `ctx.state.lastGates = cmp`. src/pipeline/context.ts:417-425 checkpoints the completed stage only after `await fn(stage)`.
verification.trigger: The daemon stops after the handle-clearing save but before the stage comparison is checkpointed. Resume has neither a completed-stage checkpoint nor an execution handle, so it starts another execution instead of attaching to the completed one.

findings.title: Landing checks never persist an execution handle
findings.detail: The landing queue calls executeGate without a persistence callback or stored handle, so its default no-op persistence is used. A restart during landing checks cannot reattach to work started by an executor and instead starts another suite. This leaves one of the explicitly required daemon gate paths outside the durability contract.
findings.suggestion: Store the landing execution handle in durable queue state before attaching, and use it when the queue resumes.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a landing suite is running on an executor. The resumed queue starts another suite, leaving the original execution untracked.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:386-401 calls `executeGate(..., this.deps.gateExecutor)` without a stored handle or persistence callback. src/gates/executor.ts:150-160 defaults these to `stored?: ExecutionHandle` and `persist ... = async () => {}`, then executes `const handle = stored ?? (await executor.start(req, signal));`. The landing resume path explicitly says `// checking re-runs the checks from the start, like a queued entry` (src/land/queue.ts:297).
verification.trigger: A daemon restart during landing checks resumes the checking entry and calls start again because no execution identity was persisted. This omits the requested durable handle contract. Local rerunning is explicitly allowed today; orphaning surviving remote work would arise with a future executor.

findings.title: Pending retry executions are discarded on restart
findings.detail: Only baseline, initial, and rebase handles are eligible for reattachment. On restart during a timeout, baseline retry, or regression retry, the stage starts over and discards the stored handle. After a daemon restart, cancelGateExecution cannot find an execution in its process-local map, so a remote execution can continue while replacement work starts. This violates the requested durable attach behavior for every gate run.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry context to resume the pending execution and attach to its stored handle without starting it again.
findings.failure_scenario: A daemon restarts while a LAN-style executor is running a regression retry. The resumed stage clears the retry handle and starts new gate work while the original retry remains active.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:25 permits stored handles only for `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"]`; lines 29-32 discard other pending handles. src/gates/executor.ts:40-43 cancels only a handle found in the current process's `liveExecutions` map. test/gate-executor.test.ts:563-567 explicitly expects retry resume to avoid the old handle and perform two new starts.
verification.trigger: Restart while an executor that survives daemon restarts is running a regression retry. The new process cannot cancel it through the process-local map, discards its handle, and starts replacement gate work.

findings.title: An attach failure clears the durable execution handle
findings.detail: A synchronous attach error calls onSettled even though the execution has not been confirmed settled. The caller consequently clears the persisted handle in its finally block. A transient attach failure or an executor initialization error can therefore lose the only identity for work that is still running, making subsequent recovery or cancellation impossible.

findings.detail: The profile grants full file reads for four filenames in every ancestor of every allowed path. findings.title: Handle shutdown failures from the abort listener
findings.detail: The abort listener discards the promise returned by stop(), but stop() rejects if process termination cannot be confirmed or scratch removal fails. That produces an unhandled rejection, which can terminate the daemon instead of reporting the cleanup failure through the run. The later caller awaiting the same promise does not reliably prevent the rejection from being reported first.
findings.suggestion: Attach a rejection handler in the abort listener and preserve the failure for the owner awaiting stop(), without removing scratch when termination is unconfirmed.
findings.failure_scenario: A preview is running when its signal is aborted, and process inspection fails during termination. stop() rejects with ProcessTerminationError while its promise is discarded by onAbort, producing an unhandled rejection.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/preview.ts:115–116: `await serving?.catch((error: unknown) => { if (error instanceof ProcessTerminationError) throw error; });`; src/pipeline/preview.ts:122–123: `const onAbort = () => { void stop(); };`. src/util/proc.ts:425–434 constructs `new ProcessTerminationError(...)` after failed shutdown inspection and calls `reject(terminationError)`.

findings.title: Cancellation during the new post-merge lookup is overwritten
findings.detail: The new lookup awaits after the merge succeeds. If the land is cancelled while that lookup is in flight, cancellation aborts its signal and records the entry as cancelled, but the catch converts the abort to null and landed() unconditionally writes the entry back to landed. A client that resolves after cancellation has the same effect.
findings.suggestion: After the lookup, re-read the entry and honor the abort or cancelled state before recording the result; make the terminal transition conditional.
findings.failure_scenario: A user cancels an active land while getGitHubPr is waiting after a successful merge; the entry changes from cancelled to landed when the lookup rejects or returns.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:257-258: `this.inFlight.get(id)?.abort(); this.finish(id, "cancelled", "cancelled");`. At :620-621 the metadata await catches rejection with `.catch(() => null)` and unconditionally calls `this.landed(...)`; :381 calls `this.finish(entry.id, "landed", ...)`. At :737, finish unconditionally calls `updateLandEntry(id, { state, reason })`.
verification.trigger: Cancel while the post-merge metadata request is pending. Whether it resolves or rejects on abort, landed() overwrites the persisted cancelled state.

findings.title: Missing merge metadata can remain missing permanently
findings.detail: If the post-merge lookup fails or returns an observation without metadata, landed() records the run as merged with null fields. Reconciliation then only examines an already-saved snapshot and never fetches this PR. With polling disabled, or with the last saved snapshot still OPEN, no later observation will fill the fields, even when GitHub has the merge information.
findings.suggestion: Provide a bounded, retryable way to obtain a confirmed merged observation when the initial metadata lookup fails, including installations without polling.
findings.failure_scenario: The merge succeeds but the following gh pr view times out, and the installation has polling disabled. The parent run retains null mergedBy and mergedAt indefinitely.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:620 catches the post-merge read failure with `.catch(() => null)`; lines 375–378 then write `merged: true` with null metadata. src/integrations/github-notifier.ts:159–168 handles already-merged runs using only `savedSnapshot(store.githubPrData(run.prUrl))`, then unconditionally `continue`s, preventing a fresh request. src/integrations/index.ts:50–57 starts no poller when `githubPoll` is false.
verification.trigger: Polling is disabled, no saved MERGED snapshot exists, and the post-merge PR read times out. A succeeded parent run is marked merged with null actor/time and subsequent reconciliation never fetches the missing metadata.

findings.title: Later metadata repair leaves the merge feed item incorrect
findings.detail: Updating only mergedBy and mergedAt does not update the existing run.merged feed item: the feed trigger captures those values when merged changes from false to true. Thus the newly added repair path can make the run record correct while the feed still reports null fields, which is the discrepancy the request identifies.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the feed exposes the confirmed metadata when it arrives, while preserving the intended event ordering and deduplication semantics.
findings.failure_scenario: The initial post-merge observation has null metadata; a later saved MERGED snapshot supplies a login and timestamp. The run is updated, but its existing run.merged feed item's data still contains null for both fields.

verification.evidence: src/db/store.ts:1821–1824: `if (current.merged && current.status !== "needs_human") { ... this.updateRun(id, { mergedBy, mergedAt }); return false; }`. src/db/migrations/20261003T2139-run-resolution.sql:7 watches only `UPDATE OF status, pr_url, merged`; lines 11–14 snapshot merge metadata into `run.merged` only `WHERE NEW.merged AND NOT OLD.merged`. src/db/store.ts:91–92 reads stored feed data directly: `SELECT ... summary, data FROM feed`.
verification.trigger: The queue records merged=true with null metadata. A later saved MERGED snapshot supplies the login and timestamp; reconciliation repairs the run row, but the existing run.merged feed item retains null values.

findings.title: A cancelled land can be overwritten after the metadata lookup
findings.detail: The new awaited lookup creates a cancellation window after the merge succeeds. If cancellation aborts the lookup, its rejection is converted to null and landed() unconditionally changes the cancelled entry to landed. A lookup that ignores the signal has the same result when it eventually returns.
findings.suggestion: After the lookup, re-read the entry and preserve a terminal cancellation before writing the land state; record the confirmed merge separately if needed.
findings.failure_scenario: A user cancels an entry while getGitHubPr is in flight after the merge command succeeds; the entry briefly becomes cancelled and is then overwritten as landed.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:254-259 allows cancellation of the active entry and writes `"cancelled"`. At :620-621, `await ... .catch(() => null)` is followed unconditionally by `this.landed(...)`; :381 and :737 write `"landed"` without checking current state or abort.
verification.trigger: Cancel an entry during the post-merge metadata lookup; its cancelled state is subsequently overwritten as landed.

findings.title: A failed metadata lookup can leave merge fields null permanently
findings.detail: The lookup failure is silently discarded and both runs are marked merged. The poller excludes merged runs from githubTracked, while reconciliation only reads an already-saved snapshot for merged runs. If that snapshot still says OPEN, no later observation fills the fields.
findings.suggestion: Provide a bounded recovery path for missing merge metadata, or persist a suitable confirmed merge observation before excluding the PR from polling.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts the merge, but the subsequent gh pr view times out or returns an OPEN observation; mergedBy and mergedAt remain null even after GitHub becomes available.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:620 converts lookup failures to null; :370-378 sets `merged: true` while metadata remains null for absent or OPEN observations. src/integrations/github-notifier.ts:159-168 only reads `savedSnapshot(store.githubPrData(run.prUrl))` for already merged runs, then executes `continue`. src/db/store.ts:2848 excludes these runs from polling with `AND NOT r.merged`.
verification.trigger: The post-merge lookup fails or returns OPEN before any MERGED snapshot is saved. The queue marks the runs merged with null metadata, excluding them from polling and fresh reconciliation requests; later GitHub recovery alone does not fill the fields.

findings.suggestion: Ensure the feed presents the recovered metadata, including for already-created merge events.
findings.failure_scenario: A queue merge initially records null metadata and a later saved MERGED snapshot supplies the actor and time; the run has the correct fields but its existing run.merged feed item still reports null for both.

verification.evidence: src/db/store.ts:1821–1824 backfills an already-merged run using `this.updateRun(id, { mergedBy, mergedAt })` and returns. src/db/migrations/20261003T2139-run-resolution.sql:7 watches only `status, pr_url, merged`; lines 11–14 capture merge metadata into the feed only `WHERE NEW.merged AND NOT OLD.merged`. src/db/store.ts:716–728 reads stored feed rows without refreshing their merge metadata.
verification.trigger: The queue records a merge with null metadata, creating a run.merged feed item. A later saved MERGED snapshot fills the run's actor/time, but the existing feed item's fields remain null, leaving the explicitly requested feed accuracy unresolved.

This leaves the specific feed inconsistency in the request unresolved for delayed observations.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the feed exposes the subsequently confirmed metadata while preserving the intended event semantics.

verification.trigger: The immediate post-merge lookup lacks metadata, then a later poll saves the merger and timestamp. The run receives both values while its persisted run.merged feed data remains null.

findings.title: Redact consumer names before recording approvals
findings.detail: The new consumer value is passed directly into recordApproval. The database stores it verbatim, and the review_approvals trigger copies it into the feed summary and data. A registered credential supplied as a consumer name therefore leaves the process and persists without redaction.
findings.suggestion: Apply credential redaction to the normalized reviewer identity before passing it to recordApproval, and cover the database and feed outputs with a test.
findings.failure_scenario: An MCP client submits an approval with consumer set to a registered API token; the token appears in review_approvals and the review.approved feed item.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/review-round.ts:196–201 constructs the reviewer with `mcpRequestedBy(parsed.data.consumer)` and passes it directly to `store.recordApproval(...)`. src/feed.ts:36 defines that helper as `(consumer: string): string => `mcp:${consumer}``, without redaction. src/db/store.ts:1522 persists it unchanged via `.run(runId, prUrl, sha, reviewer, Date.now())`. src/db/migrations/20261004T1757-review-rounds.sql:57–58 copies `NEW.reviewer` into the feed description and JSON data.
verification.trigger: Submit a valid MCP approval with consumer equal to a registered API token of at most 200 characters. The token is stored unredacted as `mcp:<token>` in review_approvals and the review.approved feed item.

findings.title: Do not overwrite a cancellation while fetching merge metadata
findings.detail: The new metadata lookup adds an await after the merge succeeds. If the land is cancelled while that lookup is pending, cancel() records cancelled and aborts the signal, but the caught lookup failure then calls landed(), which unconditionally changes the entry back to landed and emits another feed event.
findings.suggestion: Re-read the entry after the lookup and condition the terminal update on its still being in the expected merging state.
findings.failure_scenario: A merge succeeds, the PR metadata request is still pending, and a user cancels the land entry. The request aborts, but the entry changes from cancelled to landed afterward.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:620-621: `const observed = await ... .catch(() => null); this.landed(...)`. No abort or current-state check intervenes. Cancellation writes `"cancelled"` at :258, but landed writes `"landed"` through :381 and :737.
verification.trigger: Cancel during the new metadata await; after the request aborts, execution proceeds to landed() and replaces the cancellation.

findings.title: Later merge metadata does not correct the feed event
findings.detail: The request says to fill the parent run's `run.merged` fields from the recorded merge. If the queue's immediate GitHub lookup fails or returns no metadata, it emits a `run.merged` event with null fields. This later update fills the run row but does not update that event or emit a correction, so the feed retains the original disagreement permanently. The new test explicitly verifies that no further event is produced but does not check the original event's data after reconciliation.
findings.suggestion: Make the feed expose the subsequently confirmed metadata, either by correcting the existing event or by a suitable correction mechanism that preserves feed semantics.
findings.failure_scenario: The post-merge lookup returns null, then a later saved PR snapshot contains the merger and timestamp; the run row is corrected but its `run.merged` feed item still reports both as null.

verification.evidence: src/db/store.ts:1821–1824: the already-merged branch calls `this.updateRun(id, { mergedBy, mergedAt })` and returns. src/db/migrations/20261003T2139-run-resolution.sql:13–14 stores `'mergedBy', NEW.merged_by, 'mergedAt', NEW.merged_at` only `WHERE NEW.merged AND NOT OLD.merged`. src/db/store.ts:91–92 selects feed `data` directly from `feed`.
verification.trigger: A null post-merge lookup produces a merge event with null fields. A subsequent saved PR snapshot corrects the run metadata without correcting the existing merge event, leaving the requested feed accuracy unresolved.

findings.title: MCP approvals still default to human
findings.detail: The request says to record the MCP consumer instead of `reviewer: "human"`. The new consumer argument is optional, and an existing MCP approval call without it still reaches `submitReview` with neither consumer nor reviewer and records `human`. The added test explicitly expects that old behavior, so it does not establish the requested behavior for all MCP approvals.
findings.suggestion: Ensure MCP approval calls provide a consumer identity, or require one for MCP approvals and make the tool instructions explain that requirement.
findings.failure_scenario: An MCP client calls `limitless_review` with the previously documented run, verdict and reviewedSha arguments but no consumer; the resulting `review.approved` feed item still names `human`.

verification.evidence: src/feed.ts:14 declares `consumer: consumer.optional()`, reused by the MCP review schema at src/integrations/mcp.ts:323. The handler forwards input without adding provenance at src/integrations/mcp.ts:343. src/pipeline/review-round.ts:196–199 selects `parsed.data.consumer === undefined ? (parsed.data.reviewer ?? "human") : mcpRequestedBy(parsed.data.consumer)`. test/mcp-proxy.test.ts:93 explicitly expects `"human"` when consumer is omitted, and lines 98–101 assert that value in the approval feed.
verification.trigger: An MCP client submits a valid limitless_review approval with run, verdict and reviewedSha but omits consumer. The approval succeeds and its review.approved feed item still identifies the reviewer as human, leaving the requested MCP provenance correction incomplete.

findings.title: A concurrent snapshot change can report the old head as current
findings.detail: The final consistency check reports `now.sha` whenever the snapshot and recorded head disagree. If the saved snapshot advances during the awaited Git reads while the recorded head still contains the old SHA, the response calls that old SHA the current head. The request asks a changed-head error to give the new head.
findings.suggestion: Only name a head when the current observations agree on it; otherwise report the mismatch without presenting the old recorded SHA as current.
findings.failure_scenario: A read starts at head A, the saved PR snapshot advances to B during Git reads, and the recorded head remains A. The response says `current head A`.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:575–578 checks `reviewableHead(JSON.parse(current).headRefOid, {...now, pushing: ...}).headSha !== headSha` but returns `superseded(now?.sha)`. src/integrations/mcp-head.ts:13–14 returns a null head on snapshot/record disagreement. A mismatched snapshot can be saved independently: src/integrations/github-poller.ts:400–401 performs `await call(...)` followed by `if (res) save(head, [])` without rechecking the head epoch.
verification.trigger: If the saved snapshot becomes B during Git reads while the recorded head is A, the final mismatch check refuses the view but labels A as the current head. The unchecked delayed snapshot save makes divergent observations plausible, though an ordinary poll updates both records together.
