findings.title: PR numbers cannot target unowned pull requests
findings.detail: The existing CLI accepts a PR number or URL, but the unowned path accepts only a full GitHub URL. A valid number that has no matching factory run is rejected as "run not found", even when its repository is configured.
findings.suggestion: Resolve PR-number targets in the configured repository context, and report ambiguity when the repository cannot be determined.
findings.failure_scenario: Running `limitless land 7 --sha <full-head-sha>` for a hand-opened PR returns "run not found" instead of queuing it.

verification.evidence: src/cli/main.ts:573 forwards the argument unchanged: `body: JSON.stringify({ target: sub, ...(values.sha ? { sha: values.sha } : {}) })`. src/land/queue.ts:184 routes missing runs to `requestUnowned(input)`, whose lines 226–227 require a full URL: `const match = /^https:\/\/github\.com\/([^/]+\/[^/]+)\/pull\/[1-9]\d*$/.exec(input.target); if (!match) throw new Error("run not found");`.
verification.trigger: `limitless land 7 --sha <full-head-sha>` for an unowned open PR reaches the URL-only validator and throws `run not found`.

findings.title: Fork pull requests are categorically refused
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories without excluding PRs from forks. This check rejects every cross-repository PR before it can enter the queue, leaving that common class of hand-opened PR without the requested confined land path.
findings.suggestion: Support the head repository when fetching and updating the approved branch, while retaining the pinned-head and publication checks.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR from a contributor's fork targets a configured repository and has the supplied current head SHA; the request fails with "cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed".

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:251–252: `if (pr.state !== "OPEN") throw new Error(...)`; `if (pr.isCrossRepository) throw new Error("cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed");`. This rejects open fork PRs after validating that the target repository is configured at lines 228–230.
verification.trigger: An open fork PR targeting a configured repository, supplied by full URL with its exact current SHA, is refused rather than queued. The requested support for open PRs does not exclude forks.

findings.title: Rollback blocks active unowned land entries
findings.detail: Unowned entries are stored with an empty run ID in the existing queue table. After a rollback, the previous release claims these entries and requires that ID to resolve to a run; it instead marks them blocked as "run  is gone". This loses the active land's progress, including a possible already-pushed base merge, rather than preserving it for the newer release.
findings.suggestion: Keep entries that the previous release cannot process out of its claimable queue, with a migration and resume strategy that preserves active work across rollback.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned land is queued or waiting for CI when the daemon rolls back to the base release. The older queue claims the entry and permanently marks it blocked because no run has ID "".

verification.evidence: src/db/store.ts:2721 persists unowned entries as `entry.runId ?? ""`. At base 381e4384, src/db/store.ts:100 reads `run_id AS runId`; src/land/queue.ts:153 resumes active entries, and :819–821 executes `const run = this.store.getRun(entry.runId)` then `if (!run) throw new Error(`run ${entry.runId} is gone`)`. Its catch at :327 calls `this.block(...)`, and :912 persists `this.finish(id, "blocked", reason)`.
verification.trigger: Roll back while an unowned entry is queued or waiting for CI. Once its claim is available, the previous daemon claims it, fails to find run "", and persists terminal blocked state instead of resuming the land.

findings.title: Bare PR numbers cannot request an unowned land
findings.detail: The existing CLI accepts a PR number, and the request asks for `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>`, but the new path accepts only a complete GitHub URL. An unowned PR has no run through which the preceding lookup can resolve its number.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a PR number to a configured repository and canonical PR URL, refusing clearly if the repository is ambiguous.
findings.failure_scenario: `limitless land 77 --sha <current-full-sha>` returns `run not found` even when PR 77 is open on the configured repository.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:183–184: `const run = this.store.getRun(input.target) ?? this.store.runForPr(this.prRef(input.target)); if (!run) return this.requestUnowned(input);`. Lines 226–227 accept only a full GitHub PR URL and otherwise `throw new Error("run not found")`. src/cli/main.ts:573 passes `target: sub` unchanged.
verification.trigger: `limitless land 77 --sha <current-full-sha>` with no owning factory run fails the URL-only check and returns `run not found`, even when PR 77 is open on the configured repository.

findings.title: Open fork PRs are categorically refused
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories and does not exclude PRs whose head is in a fork. This check rejects every such PR before attempting the land, leaving a common class of hand-opened PRs outside the feature.
findings.suggestion: Support the fork head repository throughout checkout and any required base-merge push, or explicitly resolve this restriction against the requested scope.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR targeting a configured repository from a contributor's fork is rejected with `cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed`, even with its exact current SHA.

verification.trigger: An open contributor-fork PR targeting a configured repository is rejected before SHA approval, even when the supplied SHA equals its current head.

findings.title: Rollback blocks active unowned lands
findings.detail: The empty-string sentinel keeps the old schema writable, but the previous release reads it as a run ID and requires that run to exist. After a rollback, its queue claims an unowned entry and blocks it as a missing run instead of resuming it. This violates the requirement that the previous release remain working across deploy rollback.
findings.suggestion: Provide a rollback-compatible representation and processing strategy for active unowned entries, or prevent the previous release from claiming entries it cannot process.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned land is waiting for CI when deployment rolls back; the previous daemon claims it, looks up run `""`, and marks the entry blocked because the run is gone.

Base src/land/queue.ts:819–821 looks up that empty run ID and throws `run ${entry.runId} is gone`; :327 and :912 turn the error into persisted `blocked` state.
verification.trigger: Deployment rolls back with an unowned land waiting for CI. The previous daemon claims the entry after claim release or expiry and blocks it because run "" does not exist.

findings.suggestion: Teach the digest to resolve unowned land entries by PR URL or land ID and display their current blocked state.

findings.title: A crash during discovery leaves unrecorded descendants running
findings.detail: Cleanup persists members one at a time, but recovery only examines persisted members and never resumes marker discovery. If the daemon crashes while reading or recording the initial snapshot, or after freezing a snapshot but before discovering a newly forked descendant, any unrecorded descendants survive. Recovery deletes the partial record and permits the next invocation to start, even though those descendants can still write to the checkout.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough invocation-level discovery state before cleanup begins to resume discovery after a crash, and retain the record until the complete marked set is confirmed gone.

findings.title: The step timeout may expire after the job timeout
findings.detail: The 20-minute timer starts only after checkout, Bun setup, installation, and Git configuration, while the 25-minute job timer starts before those steps. If earlier steps take at least five minutes, GitHub can cancel the job before the helper prints the process tree and exits, recreating the missing-log failure this change is intended to prevent.
findings.suggestion: Bound the check using the remaining job time or otherwise ensure its timeout and cleanup grace expire before the job deadline, including time spent in earlier steps.
findings.failure_scenario: Earlier workflow steps take six minutes and the check hangs: the job reaches its 25-minute limit after the check has run for 19 minutes, before the helper's 20-minute timeout.

verification.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:11 sets `timeout-minutes: 25`; lines 13–18 run checkout, Bun setup, installation and Git configuration first; line 21 then runs `bash scripts/ci-check.sh 20m bun run check`. scripts/ci-check.sh:26 starts a fresh `timeout ... "$limit"` without accounting for earlier steps.
verification.trigger: Earlier steps consume six minutes, then the check hangs. The job timeout cancels it after 19 check minutes, before the helper prints timeout diagnostics. This requires unusually slow setup.

findings.title: Workflow change lacks the required audit allowance
findings.detail: The supplied deterministic audit flags this workflow modification as blocked unless the request contains an explicit `Allow: workflows` allowance. The request asks for the workflow change but does not contain that allowance, so the factory cannot deliver the change as submitted.
findings.suggestion: Obtain the required workflow allowance through the factory request before delivery.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory audits this diff with the supplied request and blocks it under the ci-config policy.

findings.title: Timeout cleanup misses detached test descendants
findings.detail: The exit trap kills only the timeout process group. Tests in this repository start subprocesses in separate process groups, including through runProcess and gate-slot, so a hung detached descendant survives both the TERM and KILL sent by this wrapper. If such a descendant retains the step's output descriptors, it can also keep the runner waiting until the outer job timeout, defeating the log-preservation goal.
findings.suggestion: Terminate the check's descendant processes, including separate process groups, and add a timeout test with a detached child that retains an output descriptor.
findings.failure_scenario: A test hangs while a detached gate-slot child remains alive with inherited stdout. The wrapper times out and exits, but that child survives its process-group kill and can keep the step's output pipe open.

verification.evidence: scripts/ci-check.sh:16 sends `kill -TERM -- -"$PPID"`; scripts/ci-check.sh:29 escalates only with `kill -KILL -- "-$check"`. Both target the wrapper's process group. src/cli/gate-slot.ts:359 starts commands with `{ stdio: "inherit", detached: true, env }`, placing them outside that group. Although src/cli/gate-slot.ts:341-346 forwards TERM via `process.kill(-child.pid, signal)`, it provides no SIGKILL escalation for that detached group.
verification.trigger: A hung test has a detached gate-slot descendant that ignores TERM, or its parent cannot forward TERM. The wrapper's final group kill misses that descendant, which retains inherited output descriptors and can prevent the CI step from completing before the outer job timeout. The process-group gap is established; this particular hang has not been reproduced.

findings.title: Add the requested workflow-level timeout check
findings.detail: The helper tests exercise short limits passed directly to the script, but no test checks the actual workflow configuration. The requested workflow-level check should verify that the check step invokes the timeout wrapper and that its limit is below the job's timeout-minutes.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that reads the workflow and verifies the configured wrapper invocation and its relationship to the outer job timeout.
findings.failure_scenario: A later edit removes the wrapper or changes its limit to 25 minutes or more; the helper tests still pass while CI can again reach the job timeout without preserving the log.

This leaves the reported failure mode unresolved when no gate, review or verification failure happens to trigger another round.

findings.title: Large text logs with terminal control characters are excluded from the size warning
findings.detail: Sizes are recorded only for blobs that pass reviewableText, which rejects control bytes such as ESC. Git can treat a UTF-8 log containing ANSI color sequences as text, but the size rule sees no size for it and emits no warning. Generated command and gate output commonly contains such sequences.
findings.suggestion: Measure new files classified as text independently of the stricter reviewable-content predicate.
findings.failure_scenario: A round adds a 200 KiB UTF-8 build log containing ANSI color escape sequences outside a root hidden directory. It receives no large-text-addition warning.

verification.evidence: src/git/repos.ts:560 rejects control bytes: `if (byte === 0x7f || (byte < 0x20 && ![9, 10, 12, 13].includes(byte))) return false;`. src/git/repos.ts:1150 excludes those files from sizes: `.filter((path) => contents.get(afterText.blobs.get(path) ?? "")?.reviewable)`. src/gates/audit.ts:297 uses `(diff.headTextSizes?.[f.path] ?? 0) > 102_400`. ANSI ESC (0x1b) therefore prevents the warning.
verification.trigger: Add a 200 KiB UTF-8 log containing ANSI color escapes outside a root hidden directory. Its size is omitted, so no large-text-addition warning appears.

findings.title: Encoded credentials in filenames escape diagnostic redaction
findings.detail: The new publication diagnostic passes a Git-controlled path to `redactCredentials` without decoding it first. That function replaces only literal credential variants, so a percent-encoded credential remains recoverable in the error message. The new audit filename handling in `src/gates/audit.ts` has the same issue: `redactGateOutput` also performs literal credential redaction. These diagnostics can be stored as events or sent back to an implementer.
findings.suggestion: Decode supported filename encodings before credential redaction, or suppress the filename when its decoded forms contain a credential. Apply the same handling to both audit findings and publication diagnostics.

candidates.title: Large text logs with terminal control characters are excluded from the size warning

findings.title: Review eval calls are attributed to one provider and counted as one invocation
findings.detail: Review systems can invoke several finders, samples, and verifiers, including models on different providers. Their trial totals combine those calls, but the fallback creates one record using the trial's primary provider and model. This assigns other providers' tokens and costs to the primary provider and undercounts invocations.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate individual stored call evidence where available, and represent unattributable combined work explicitly rather than assigning it all to the primary provider.

findings.title: Implementation evals lose stored cache token totals

Because the summation returns null if any row is unknown, one implementation eval also makes the corresponding provider totals unknown.
findings.suggestion: Use the stored trial cache totals when they can be attributed, including single-round trials, and preserve known aggregate totals where per-round splits cannot be recovered.

findings.title: Long failing test names can disappear from the excerpt
findings.detail: When an assertion line is followed by a Bun failure line, the excerpt takes the end of the intervening text. If the failure line alone exceeds the remaining budget, this discards its beginning, including the `(fail)` marker and the beginning of the selected signature. The fix round then receives an excerpt that does not identify the failing test.
findings.suggestion: Reserve space for the beginning of the selected signature line before filling the remaining excerpt budget with assertion and stack context.
findings.failure_scenario: A Bun log contains `error: assertion failed` followed by a `(fail)` line whose test name is longer than 2,000 characters. The signature contains the beginning of that line, but the excerpt contains only its tail.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts:107 uses `window(start + 1, index + 1, Math.max(0, 1999 - head.length), true)`; line 98 implements this as `Math.max(left, right - limit)`, retaining the tail rather than the beginning of the selected failure line. A direct probe returned an excerpt without `(fail) real failure`.
verification.trigger: An assertion error followed by a failing test title over 2,000 characters produces a signature naming the test but an excerpt containing the assertion and only the title's trailing characters.

findings.title: Change substantially exceeds the requested line budget
findings.detail: The request budgets about 80 lines including tests; the diff adds 354 lines and removes 36, including a new windowed redaction API in a shared utility. This makes the change substantially larger to review and maintain than the stated scope permits.
findings.suggestion: Reduce the implementation and tests to the requested scope, or explicitly explain the necessary overrun.

findings.title: An unrelated later test failure can replace the first error as the signature
findings.detail: When the first failure-shaped line starts with `error:`, the search advances to any later `(fail)` line unless another failure-shaped or passing line intervenes. It does not establish that the lines belong to the same Bun assertion block. For a build error followed by a test failure, the signature identifies the later test and the excerpt combines evidence from two failures, potentially discarding the later test's diagnostic. A targeted check, `bun -e 'import {ciSignature} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; console.log(ciSignature("test", "error: first failure\n"+"x".repeat(3000)+"\n(fail) second failure", "fallback"));'`, returned `line: "(fail) second failure"` with an excerpt starting `error: first failure`.
findings.suggestion: Associate an assertion with a following Bun test name only when the intervening output establishes that they belong to the same failure; otherwise retain the first error line.
findings.failure_scenario: A job logs `error: first failure`, then ordinary output, then `(fail) second failure`; the record and fix-round signature identify the second failure while the excerpt begins with the first.

verification.trigger: `error: first failure`, ordinary output, then an unrelated `(fail) second failure` causes the later test to replace the first error as the signature without establishing that they belong to the same assertion block.

findings.title: Preserve event sequence across job attempts
findings.detail: Each attempt starts its event sequence at zero, but agent_job_events is keyed by job ID and sequence, and the coordinator silently ignores conflicts. A retried job therefore loses batches whose sequence numbers overlap an earlier attempt, while later batches can be mixed with the earlier attempt's events.
findings.suggestion: Make event storage and sequencing attempt-aware, or otherwise ensure a retry cannot collide with previously stored batches.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker A posts batch 0 and then fails; worker B retries the same job and posts its own batch 0. The coordinator returns success but retains worker A's batch and discards worker B's.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:469-470 initializes each execution with `let posts = Promise.resolve(), seq = 0`. src/db/workers.ts:342 inserts events with `ON CONFLICT(job_id,seq) DO NOTHING`. src/db/workers.ts:355-359 requeues the same job using `j.attempt < 2 ? "queued" : "failed"` without clearing its events.
verification.trigger: Worker A stores batch 0 and fails. Worker B leases the same job and starts at sequence 0; its batch is silently discarded while the endpoint returns success.

findings.title: Report failure when an event batch is rejected
findings.detail: A rejected events request aborts the job controller. The catch block then skips the failure endpoint because jobSignal is aborted, so the coordinator continues to hold the lease until it expires instead of recording the rejected batch as a job failure.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish an event-post failure from cancellation and report it with a separate bounded signal before releasing the job.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator rejects an oversized or invalid event batch with HTTP 400. The harness is aborted, but no failure is posted and the job remains leased until expiry.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:273-276 throws for HTTP responses below 500. At :480, `posts.catch(() => agentJobs.get(id)?.controller.abort())` aborts the job on event rejection. At :533-538, failure reporting is guarded by `if (!jobSignal.aborted)`.
verification.trigger: An event batch receives HTTP 400 or 413 while the lease is valid. The rejection aborts the harness and suppresses the failure notification, leaving coordinator state leased until expiry.

findings.title: Fence at the lease deadline rather than the next interval
findings.detail: The periodic check can run almost one heartbeat interval after the lease period has elapsed. During that window the coordinator can expire and reassign the job while the original worker continues running the harness and spending quota.
findings.suggestion: Schedule fencing against the last successful heartbeat's actual deadline and reset that deadline on each success.
findings.failure_scenario: A heartbeat succeeds just after a fence tick and connectivity is then lost. The tick immediately before the deadline sees a fresh heartbeat, and the worker continues until the following tick, potentially nearly another heartbeat interval after lease expiry.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:314 records `lastHeartbeat = performance.now()`. At :552-557, fencing uses `setInterval` with `if (performance.now() - lastHeartbeat > leaseMs)` and interval `Math.min(options.heartbeatMs ?? timing.heartbeat, leaseMs)`.
verification.trigger: The lease deadline falls just after a fence tick during a partition. The agent continues until the next tick, exceeding one lease period without a successful heartbeat by nearly one heartbeat interval.

findings.title: Report a failure when an event batch is rejected
findings.detail: A rejected events request aborts the job controller. The resulting error reaches the catch block with `jobSignal.aborted` already true, so it skips the failure POST and removes the job from the worker's held list. The coordinator retains the lease until expiry, and the rejection is lost instead of immediately failing the attempt. The new rejection test checks only that the job is not done, so it does not detect this.
findings.suggestion: Track event-post failures separately from cancellation, abort the harness, and report the failure using a bounded signal that is not already aborted.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator returns HTTP 400 or 413 for an event batch while the lease is still valid; the harness stops, but the job remains leased until its lease expires.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:480 aborts on rejected event posts: `posts.catch(() => agentJobs.get(id)?.controller.abort())`. At :533-538, `if (!jobSignal.aborted)` prevents posting `/failure`. src/server/workers.ts:210 limits event bodies to 1 MiB, and :275 returns 413 for `BodyTooLarge`.
verification.trigger: A validly leased agent sends an oversized or invalid batch and receives HTTP 413 or 400. Its harness stops, but no failure is reported; the lease remains until expiry.

verification.trigger: A partition follows a successful heartbeat whose timing is just after a fence tick. With defaults, the agent can continue for nearly 70 seconds after that heartbeat instead of stopping at the 60-second deadline.

The job is omitted from heartbeat renewals, expires, and its eventual result is rejected.

findings.title: Cancel the open job when reconciliation fails
findings.detail: If `publication.resume()` throws, the error is propagated while the queued or leased job remains open. The engine can then finish the run as NeedsHuman, but the worker continues executing and can push after the coordinator has stopped waiting for its report. Orphan cleanup only runs at factory start or stop, so it does not close this window.
findings.suggestion: After re-reading the job and handling a concurrently completed result, conditionally cancel an open job before propagating the reconciliation error.
findings.failure_scenario: A resumed leased job is still running when the coordinator's git status command or private-strings read fails. Reconciliation throws, the run ends NeedsHuman, and the worker later pushes a commit.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:75-79 awaits `publication.resume(request)`, then on exception only checks abortion and a completed job before `throw error`; it never cancels the open job. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1143-1144 converts reconciliation errors into `NeedsHumanError`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:448-450 records the terminal status without cancelling worker jobs.
verification.trigger: A matching, leased job encounters a git or private-strings read error during reconciliation. The coordinator exits reconciliation with NeedsHuman while the worker job remains leased and can continue publishing changes.

findings.title: Check for an unreported push before falling back after reconciliation
findings.detail: A failed resume check cancels the old job and goes straight to `prepare()`. If the worktree is dirty, or the remote lookup fails, `prepare()` returns null and the executor runs locally without checking whether the cancelled worker already pushed. The existing failed-job path checks the remote before local fallback; this new path bypasses that protection and can continue a run with an unaccepted worker commit on its branch.
findings.suggestion: After cancelling an unreconciled job, verify the branch against the stored request before permitting a local fallback; treat an unavailable remote check as an unresolved failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes but its report has not been accepted. After restart, the coordinator worktree is dirty, so resume fails, the job is cancelled, prepare returns null, and a local session runs instead of stopping for the unreported push.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:89-91 cancels the open job and clears `id` after a failed resume check. It then calls `publication.prepare()` at line 97 and `if (!prepared) return fallback()` at line 110; fallback calls `local()` at line 51. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1148-1150 executes `if (!(await clean())) return null` before reading the remote. The unreported-push guard at src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:205-208 is therefore bypassed.
verification.trigger: A resumed worker job has pushed a commit without an accepted report, and the coordinator worktree is dirty. Reconciliation cancels the job, prepare returns null before checking the remote, and a local session runs instead of stopping NeedsHuman for the unreported push.

findings.title: Keep explicitly local panel finders on the coordinator
findings.detail: The shared review call supplies checkout metadata to every production panel finder, while worker eligibility has no indication that a finder was configured as local. findings.suggestion: Add a test exercising the CLI dependency wiring with a stored run of non-default complexity and assert that the generated case retains it.
findings.failure_scenario: The fixture's fake lookup returns small and the test passes, while invoking the documented command for the same run writes medium.

verification.evidence: test/implement-replay-cases.test.ts:209 defaults fixture complexity to "small"; lines 218–220 inject `lookupRun: async (id) => { expect(id).toBe("r1"); return { complexity }; }`. scripts/implement-replay-cases.ts:386–402 supplies only `cache` to the CLI's `generateReplayCases` call, omitting `lookupRun`. Lines 69–73 leave complexity null without that dependency, and line 93 returns `complexity: complexity ?? "medium"`.
verification.trigger: Generate a valid replay whose production run has complexity small: the injected fixture lookup produces small, but the documented CLI supplies no lookup and writes medium. The test does not cover this wiring discrepancy.

findings.title: Head validation exposes the shared repository cache to PR test code
findings.detail: The head checkout is a linked worktree of the shared cache. Gate confinement explicitly grants linked worktrees read access to their Git common directory, and the sandbox permits outbound network access. Consequently, setup commands and hidden tests from the PR can read objects and refs from the entire cache, including unrelated branches and retained eval solutions, and send them outside the sandbox. The base validation uses an isolated snapshot, but head validation bypasses that isolation.
findings.suggestion: Validate head in a standalone repository containing only the required pinned snapshot, without granting access to the shared cache or unrelated history.
findings.failure_scenario: A merged PR contains a test that reads another cached branch with Git and sends its contents to an external endpoint. Running the generator executes that test in the linked head worktree with read access to the cache.

verification.evidence: scripts/implement-replay-cases.ts:272 creates head with `addDetachedWorktree(repository, item.head, cwd, signal)` and :281 runs its hidden tests. src/harness/scratch.ts:180-184 validates the shared `commondir` then grants `readable.push(record, ...paths.slice(1))`. src/harness/sandbox.ts:54-56 uses `(allow default)` and restricts outbound networking only to the daemon's localhost port.
verification.trigger: A selected merged PR's test reads other refs/objects through the linked worktree's shared Git common directory and transmits their contents externally. Head validation grants the necessary cache read access and outbound networking.

findings.title: The generator cannot run from this checkout because its dataset is absent
findings.detail: The requested command reads the default implement dataset before processing any PR, but this checkout contains no evals/implement directory or cases.json. Every invocation therefore exits with ENOENT before fetching or validating a PR. The new tests supply a separate temporary casePath and do not exercise the CLI's default path.
findings.suggestion: Make the required existing dataset available to the command, or provide a supported initialization or dataset-location mechanism consistent with the runner.
findings.failure_scenario: Running the documented generator in a fresh checkout fails while reading evals/implement/cases.json and produces no table or cases.

verification.evidence: scripts/implement-replay-cases.ts:122-123 uses `deps.casePath ?? defaultCasePath("implement")` followed immediately by `readFileSync(casePath, "utf8")`. src/evals/cases.ts:269 resolves this to `../../evals/${role}/cases.json`. HEAD's root tree contains no `evals` directory. scripts/implement-replay-cases.ts:404 prints the table only after generation returns.
verification.trigger: Run the documented generator in this fresh checkout: the missing evals/implement/cases.json causes an immediate read failure, so no cases or results table are produced.

findings.title: The CLI never looks up available production complexity
findings.detail: The request requires the production run's triage complexity when it can be found. Although the generator accepts a lookupRun dependency and the store exposes run records, the only requested CLI entry point never supplies that dependency. Consequently every generated case defaults to medium, even when the report identifies a locally available run with a different complexity.
findings.suggestion: Wire a read-only run-record lookup into the CLI and retain the documented fallback only when the record or complexity is unavailable.
findings.failure_scenario: A merged PR's footer names a locally stored run whose complexity is small; the generated case records medium instead.

verification.evidence: scripts/implement-replay-cases.ts:71-73 looks up complexity only under `if (runId && lookupRun)`; :93 otherwise returns `complexity: complexity ?? "medium"`. The CLI dependency object at :386-402 supplies only `cache`. docs/EVALS.md:372 explicitly states, `The CLI has no run-record lookup`.
verification.trigger: A PR footer identifies an available local production run with complexity small. CLI generation never queries that record and assigns medium, missing the requested available production complexity.

findings.title: The replay-v2 tag cannot select the generated cases
findings.detail: The request says each case is tagged replay-v2 so a v2 eval selects them with --cases. The change adds the tag, but --cases is still interpreted exclusively as case IDs: the selection code validates each argument as an ID and filters on item.id. Thus --cases replay-v2 cannot select the generated group.
findings.suggestion: Support selecting cases by the replay-v2 tag through --cases, while retaining existing ID selection.
findings.failure_scenario: After generating several replay cases, running an implement eval with --cases replay-v2 rejects the selector rather than running those cases.

verification.evidence: scripts/implement-replay-cases.ts:94 adds `"replay-v2"` to tags. src/cli/eval.ts:158 converts `--cases` into `caseIds`. src/evals/cases.ts:435-437 checks `c.id === id`, throws `Unknown case ID: ${id}` otherwise, and filters exclusively by case ID.
verification.trigger: After generating cases tagged replay-v2, run an implement eval with `--cases replay-v2`. Selection rejects it as an unknown case ID instead of selecting the generated cases.

Verifier: 11 candidates, 11 checked, 0 refuted.

findings.title: Do not record a snapshot result after its checkout changes HEAD
findings.detail: The snapshot gate result is recorded under the original tree without checking whether setup or the test changed the snapshot checkout's HEAD. The gates stage checks HEAD only in the separate session checkout, so it cannot detect this change. A passing result can consequently be reused and accepted as verification evidence for a tree the test did not check.
findings.suggestion: Check the snapshot checkout's HEAD after execution and retries, and refuse to record evidence if it no longer identifies the snapshot commit.
findings.failure_scenario: A test command checks out another commit containing a passing test, runs it successfully, and exits zero. The record is stored under the original snapshot tree and reused for the round commit.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:134 computes the key before execution: `const key = await agentGateKey(ctx, checkout, tree)`. Lines 189–193 store `comparison` when `completed(result)` without rechecking checkout HEAD. The completed predicate at lines 55–62 checks exit status and confinement only. src/git/repos.ts:562–573 copies history and refs into the writable snapshot repository, making other commits available.
verification.trigger: A candidate test checks out an available passing commit and exits successfully. Its result is recorded under the original snapshot tree and subsequently reused for that tree.

findings.title: Apply the gates stage's timeout retry before returning the session result
findings.detail: The session path calls retryRegressions but does not perform the gates stage's timeout-only rerun. Timed-out results are then excluded from storage, so the session immediately receives a failure and the gates stage runs the suite again even on the identical tree. This loses the normal timeout retry and classification and defeats the requested reuse for this failure mode.
findings.suggestion: Share the gates stage's timeout handling with the session gate path and persist the resulting completed execution and retry information.
findings.failure_scenario: The first test attempt times out transiently and would pass on the normal timeout rerun. The implementer sees a failure, and the gates stage starts the full suite again instead of reusing the factory execution.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:158 runs `const after = await run()` and then calls `retryRegressions` at line 176. src/gates/run.ts:470 explicitly excludes `c.result.timedOut` from that retry. src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:61 also excludes timed-out results from persistence. In contrast, src/pipeline/engine.ts:1560–1571 detects `timeoutOnly` and reruns gates from the committed tree.
verification.trigger: The session's factory test attempt times out while the baseline did not. No normal timeout retry occurs, the session receives failure, and no reusable record exists; the gates stage runs the suite again.

findings.title: Preserve worker-session behavior when the repository selects gate mode
findings.detail: The new gate mode is translated to refuse for worker sessions. The request limits the new behavior to local implement sessions and says worker implement rounds retain their existing behavior. Previously, an implementer in slot mode could run its full suite under a slot; with this repository switched to gate, the same worker request is now refused.
findings.suggestion: Keep the existing worker full-suite behavior when translating the local-only gate policy.
findings.failure_scenario: A LAN worker runs an implement round for this repository and invokes bun test. The wrapper rejects the command instead of running it in the existing slotted lane.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:153 maps worker policy using `agentFullSuite: call.agentFullSuite === "gate" ? "refuse" : call.agentFullSuite`. src/workers/client.ts:881 passes `{ role: req.role, agentFullSuite: req.agentFullSuite }` to the wrapper. src/cli/agent-test.ts:229 checks `lane === "gate" && config.role === "implement" && config.agentFullSuite === "refuse"`, prints `full suite refused`, and returns `1` at line 237.
verification.trigger: A LAN worker implement session receives this repository's gate policy and invokes a slotted full-suite command such as bun test. The policy becomes refuse, so the wrapper rejects the command instead of running it in the existing slotted lane, violating the explicit requirement to preserve worker behavior.

findings.title: Return failure when confinement fails with exit status zero
findings.detail: The command status is derived from the process exit code without checking result.ok or confinementFailed(result). The gate runner can mark a result as a confinement failure even when the shell exits zero. In that case the wrapper reports a successful command to the implementer despite the failed isolation check.
findings.suggestion: Return a nonzero status whenever confinementFailed(result) is true, including for a failed setup step.
findings.failure_scenario: A setup or test command emits the confinement failure detected by the gate runner, then exits zero. The factory prints FAIL but the wrapper exits 0, so a script or agent treats the failed security check as successful.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:132 computes `ok = !confinementError && res.exitCode === 0 && !res.timedOut && !res.cancelled`, while line 139 preserves `exitCode: res.exitCode`. src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:198 returns `result.exitCode` unless timed out, null, or greater than 128; line 200 prints FAIL based on `result.ok`. src/cli/agent-test.ts:223 returns that status unchanged.
verification.trigger: A setup or test process emits a detected confinement-failure signature and exits zero. The result is correctly marked failed and not cached, but the wrapper prints FAIL and returns success to its caller.

findings.title: A synthetic commit can make a reused gate pass on a different Git state
findings.detail: The snapshot checkout uses a synthetic commit whose message and SHA differ from the round commit, and always adds a child commit even when the tree equals HEAD. Gate commands can inspect Git history or HEAD, so a test may pass in the snapshot checkout but fail in the eventual round checkout. Reuse is keyed only by tree and then suppresses that test at the gates stage.
findings.suggestion: Ensure gate checks observe the same relevant Git state as the round checkout, or refuse reuse when that equivalence cannot be established.
findings.failure_scenario: A test checks the latest commit message or the number of commits since a tag. It passes against the synthetic 'Factory gate snapshot' commit but would fail against the actual round commit; the matching tree causes the passing result to be reused.

verification.evidence: src/git/repos.ts:548–553 creates `commit-tree tree -p HEAD` with `stdin: "Factory gate snapshot\n"`; line 568 installs that commit as snapshot HEAD. The actual round uses `commitAll(cwd, commitMessage(ctx, round))` (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1404), whose message is `limitless: ${ctx.run.title}...` (line 773). Reuse keys only `{ runId, treeHash, gatesHash, envHash }` (src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:86); engine.ts:1525–1527 then removes the reused test from execution.
verification.trigger: A Git-metadata-dependent test passes with the synthetic snapshot commit message but fails with the actual round message. With unchanged files, the tree matches and the passing snapshot result suppresses the failing round test. This requires an unusual metadata-dependent check; ordinary commit counts remain equal when both commits share the same parent.

findings.title: Exercise verify substitution through a reused execution
findings.detail: The integration test stops after checking that reused metadata reaches gate evidence. The added substitution test separately fabricates a GateEvidence object, so neither test proves that a real reused execution is accepted by verify, or that session-produced output is rejected there.
findings.suggestion: Add fake-harness pipeline cases that reach verify with a reused factory execution and with only a session claim, then assert the respective criterion outcomes.
findings.failure_scenario: The gates stage records reused metadata but verify discards it or accepts an agent's printed success claim; the current tests can still pass.

verification.evidence: test/agent-full-suite-gate.test.ts:216–218 only asserts `state.gateEvidence?.checks.find((c) => c.name === "test")?.result.reused` equals the artifact metadata. test/gate-evidence.test.ts:133–137 separately constructs synthetic evidence with `const evidence = gates();` and `check.result.reused = ...` before calling `resolve(blocked, evidence)`. Neither exercises verify substitution using the actual reused execution.
verification.trigger: A regression in passing actual reused gate evidence into verify can leave the metadata assertions and synthetic substitution test passing. This confirms an integration test gap, not a demonstrated runtime failure.

findings.title: Test changes to the actual gate configuration and environment
findings.detail: The configuration and environment mismatch scenarios directly overwrite the stored hash with a literal. They test database lookup, but would still pass if the key calculation stopped incorporating the actual gate configuration or environment.
findings.suggestion: Change a gate configuration input and a gate-relevant environment input between recording and lookup, and assert that each causes a normal test gate execution.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression makes the configuration or environment digest constant, causing an execution to be reused after its inputs change; the existing mismatch scenarios still miss because they manually alter the stored hash.

verification.evidence: test/agent-full-suite-gate.test.ts:172–175 implements both mismatch scenarios by executing `UPDATE agent_gate_executions SET ${scenario === "config" ? "gates_hash" : "env_hash"} = 'different'`. It changes neither the actual gate configuration nor the environment used by `agentGateKey`.
verification.trigger: If agentGateKey stops incorporating configuration or environment changes, these scenarios still force a database-key mismatch and pass, leaving that regression undetected.

findings.title: Do not follow candidate-controlled lockfile symlinks in the daemon
findings.detail: The new gate key hashes lockfiles from the exported candidate checkout using lockfileHash, which follows symlinks and reads their targets synchronously in the daemon, outside gate confinement. A candidate can therefore make the daemon read arbitrary accessible paths or block indefinitely on a special file. The same lookup also occurs when deciding whether to reuse a result.
findings.suggestion: Hash the lockfile blob from the Git tree, or validate with lstat that each lockfile is a regular file before reading it without following symlinks.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer commits bun.lock as a symlink to /dev/zero and requests the full suite. Computing the gate key reads an unbounded stream synchronously, potentially exhausting daemon memory or blocking the daemon.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:79 calls `lockfileHash(cwd)` on the exported candidate checkout before executing the confined gate. src/gates/cache.ts:124 performs `if (existsSync(path)) hash.update(`${name}\0`).update(readFileSync(path)).update("\0")` without checking symlinks, file type, or size. src/git/repos.ts:575 exports the candidate tree into that checkout.
verification.trigger: The candidate contains bun.lock as a symlink to /dev/zero. Key computation follows the symlink and synchronously reads an unbounded stream in the daemon, blocking it and potentially exhausting memory.

findings.title: Include the test worker count in the environment key
findings.detail: gateEnv sets LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS, but gateEnvDigest does not include that variable unless it is explicitly configured in baseline_env. A persisted result can therefore be reused after a daemon restart with a different test worker count, even though parallelism can change test outcomes.
findings.suggestion: Include LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS in the environment digest used for agent gate executions.
findings.failure_scenario: The in-session suite passes with LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS=1, then the daemon restarts with LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS=8 before the gates stage. The environment hash remains the same and the earlier pass suppresses the test run despite the changed environment.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:98 injects `LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS: String(resolveTestWorkers())` into the gate environment. src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:84 hashes it through `gateEnvDigest(env, ctx.deps.cfg.baselineEnv)`. src/gates/cache.ts:135–136 includes only `GATE_ENV_VARS`, explicit extras, or matching prefixes; LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS matches none of the defaults at lines 56–97. src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:97–99 retrieves the recorded execution using that key.
verification.trigger: With the default baseline_env configuration, the daemon restarts with a different LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS value but the same build, tree, and other key inputs. The environment hash remains unchanged, allowing the prior pass to suppress testing at the new concurrency.

findings.title: Record gate evidence without checking that the snapshot HEAD stayed unchanged
findings.detail: The request permits verification to use a factory gate execution only for the same tree. Unlike the normal gates stage, this path records the result without checking whether the gate changed HEAD. Repository-controlled test code can reset the independent checkout to another commit, run its tests, and return success; the result is then stored under the original snapshot tree and can be reused as verification evidence for code that was never tested.

findings.title: Rollback to the previous release does not notify the executor
findings.detail: The executor detects a release change only through the database setting written by this new daemon. The previous release never writes that setting, so rolling back leaves the new release SHA in place. A running new executor continues its job and can continue leasing queued jobs even though the active daemon is now the older release.
findings.suggestion: Use release ownership that the previous release can invalidate or otherwise ensure that a rollback stops the executor before the old daemon resumes work.
findings.failure_scenario: Start an in-place gate on this release, then roll back and start the base-commit daemon. The setting still names this release, so the executor does not cancel the gate as required.

verification.evidence: src/cli/daemon.ts:50 adds `factory.store.setSetting("executor.daemonRelease", factory.bootSha);`; the base daemon has no such write (base src/cli/daemon.ts:50 starts with `detachSlots = await attachSlotPools(...)`). src/gates/inplace.ts:39 detects release changes solely through `store.getSetting("executor.daemonRelease", "") !== releaseSha`. src/db/workers.ts:388 uses the same persisted setting to permit leasing.
verification.trigger: Run an executor gate on this release, then roll back to the base daemon, with no LAN worker polling to invalidate the job. The old daemon leaves executor.daemonRelease unchanged, so the executor continues the gate and can lease remaining queued jobs despite the daemon release changing.

findings.title: Process existence is treated as a fresh executor heartbeat
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only PID and birth identity; there is no heartbeat timestamp. An executor whose event loop is stalled remains eligible indefinitely. Once its lease expires, the daemon marks the job failed, but waitStopped waits indefinitely while that process exists, so it cannot fall back or proceed with the worktree.
findings.suggestion: Track and check executor heartbeat freshness, and provide a bounded, safe path for confirming that an unresponsive executor's gate processes have stopped.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor is alive but paused or blocked while running a gate. Its lease expires; the daemon enters waitStopped and never completes the gate or starts the fallback.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:359 identifies availability solely with `return processBirthSync(e.pid) === e.birth;`. Lease expiry marks the job failed (src/db/workers.ts:671–672), but fallback first calls `await workers.waitStopped(handle.id, controller.signal)` (src/gates/lan.ts:131). In waitStopped, recovery occurs only when `!worker || !this.executor(worker, false)` (src/db/workers.ts:370); otherwise it repeatedly sleeps (line 384).
verification.trigger: A leased executor remains alive but stops progressing beyond lease expiry. The job fails, but fallback waits indefinitely until the executor resumes or exits.

findings.title: Targeted and timeout retry jobs cannot reattach
findings.detail: The resume predicate explicitly accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A restart during an in-place targeted or timeout retry therefore cancels the still-running job and repeats work instead of attaching to its matching handle.
findings.suggestion: Persist and restore the retry context needed to validate and reattach matching retry jobs.
findings.failure_scenario: A daemon restarts while a long targeted retry is leased by the executor. On resume, the purpose fails this allowlist and the retry is cancelled or started again.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:30 requires '["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)'; lines 35–43 cancel and clear rejected handles. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1566 runs purpose "timeout", and lines 1592–1595 run "regression-retry-targeted" or "regression-retry". On restart, engine.ts:1536 first calls resumeGateExecution with "initial", rejecting a surviving retry handle.
verification.trigger: The daemon restarts during an in-place targeted or timeout retry. Resume cancels the surviving retry and restarts gate work instead of attaching to its result.

findings.title: LAN configuration bypasses the in-place executor for local fallback
findings.detail: When the gate executor is configured as LAN, this factory always returns the LAN executor, even when the in-place executor is enabled. Its local path for repositories outside the LAN list runs directly in the daemon, so those local gates cannot survive a daemon restart.
findings.suggestion: Route the LAN executor's local path through the in-place executor when it is enabled and available.
findings.failure_scenario: Enable the executor, configure LAN gates for one repository, and run a gate in another repository. The gate runs in the daemon and is lost on restart despite a live in-place executor.

verification.evidence: src/gates/executor.ts:77–81 uses the flag only for local routing: `return inplace && workers ? lanExecutor(workers, [], true) : localExecutor();`; the LAN branch returns `lanExecutor(workers, repos)`. src/gates/lan.ts:16 defaults `inplace = false`, and :71 routes excluded repositories directly to `local.start(req, signal)`. That executor stores executions in process-local maps (src/gates/executor.ts:85–90).
verification.trigger: Set gates.executor="lan", enable executor.enabled, configure workers.repos for one repository, and run gates in another with a fresh in-place executor available. Gates run inside the daemon instead of creating durable in-place jobs; a daemon restart loses the execution and repeats the work.

findings.title: Confinement failures are converted into local retries
findings.detail: The executor catches every error from executeGate and records an ordinary failed job. The attaching daemon then reruns every failed in-place job locally. This loses the distinction between an infrastructure failure and a ConfinementError, so a failed isolation check can be followed by a successful gate instead of failing closed.
findings.suggestion: Persist a failure classification and propagate confinement and inspection failures to the daemon without retrying them.
findings.failure_scenario: The executor's confinement preflight throws ConfinementError, but the daemon's subsequent local preflight succeeds; the gate passes despite the original security check failing.

verification.evidence: src/gates/inplace.ts:70–71 catches every error with `workers.fail(job.id, redactCredentials(String(error)))`, losing the ConfinementError type. src/db/workers.ts:626–632 sets in-place jobs to `state='failed'`. src/gates/lan.ts:130–139 handles every failed job by calling `local.start(request, controller.signal)` without checking the failure classification; lines 147–150 complete the job and return the fallback result.
verification.trigger: Executor confinement preflight throws ConfinementError; process cleanup completes; the daemon's local preflight succeeds. The local gate can pass and replace the confinement failure with a successful result.

findings.title: A cleanup failure can leave the run waiting indefinitely
findings.detail: waitStopped only attempts recovery or reports an error after the executor process disappears. If a job finishes with process discovery or cleanup records remaining, the executor deliberately leaves stopped=0 but continues running. waitStopped then polls forever because the executor is still alive, even though that executor will never revisit the completed job.
findings.suggestion: Make the executor publish a terminal cleanup failure, or have waitStopped detect that the job is no longer being cleaned up and fail closed with a clear error.
findings.failure_scenario: A cancelled gate leaves a cleanup record after process cleanup fails; the executor continues polling for other jobs, while the daemon waits forever to start the replacement gate.

verification.evidence: src/gates/inplace.ts:76–80 sets `stopped=1` only when both process discovery and cleanup lists are empty, then returns to the polling loop (line 29). src/db/workers.ts:370 permits recovery only when `!worker || !this.executor(worker, false)`; a live executor instead causes repeated sleeps (line 384).
verification.trigger: Cleanup fails and leaves a record after cancellation. The executor continues polling, while the daemon waits for stopped=1. No code retries cleanup or reports the unresolved cleanup to that waiter while the executor remains alive.

findings.title: Worktree exclusion is not atomic across concurrent starts
findings.detail: The query for existing jobs and the later enqueue are separate operations. Two daemon-side starts for the same worktree can both observe no existing job and enqueue independently. With two executor processes, each can lease one job and run both gates in the same worktree.
findings.suggestion: Enforce worktree exclusivity atomically in the database when creating or leasing an in-place job.
findings.failure_scenario: Two concurrent gate starts for the same cwd pass the existing-job query before either enqueues, and two executors lease their jobs concurrently.

verification.evidence: src/gates/lan.ts:54–60 queries existing jobs for cwd and waits only for those returned. findings.title: Rollback to an older daemon does not stop the executor
findings.detail: The executor detects a release change only through the persistent `executor.daemonRelease` setting. A daemon from before this change never updates that setting, so after rollback it still contains the newer release SHA. The newer executor continues its running job while the older daemon resumes the run without understanding the in-place handle, allowing both releases to operate on the same worktree.
findings.suggestion: Use a coordinator release and liveness mechanism that also detects replacement by a daemon that does not write this setting, and stop the executor's jobs before the older daemon can resume them.
findings.failure_scenario: A new-release in-place gate is running when the daemon is rolled back to the base release. The old daemon leaves the setting unchanged and starts its own recovery or gate while the executor continues.

verification.evidence: src/gates/inplace.ts:39 detects release changes solely with `store.getSetting("executor.daemonRelease", "") !== releaseSha`; lines 52–57 otherwise renew the lease. src/cli/daemon.ts:50 introduces `factory.store.setSetting("executor.daemonRelease", factory.bootSha)`. The base version of startScopedDaemon has no corresponding write, so rollback leaves the new release's value intact.
verification.trigger: Roll back while a new-release executor job is running. The base daemon never updates the release setting, so the executor continues renewing and running instead of cancelling as required.

findings.title: Targeted retries cannot reattach after restart
findings.detail: The resume predicate accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A running `regression-retry-targeted` job therefore gets cancelled on restart even when its stage, round, SHA, environment, release, and lease still match. The stage repeats work instead of attaching to the retry, contrary to the requested coverage of targeted retries.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry progress to resume the targeted retry at its recorded purpose and attach to its matching job.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a long targeted regression retry is running. On resume, the saved handle fails the purpose check and the running job is cancelled.

findings.title: A live but unresponsive executor can block a worktree indefinitely
findings.detail: Executor freshness is determined solely by whether its PID and birth time still match; there is no heartbeat. If the executor is alive but no longer making progress, the sweep eventually fails its lease, but `waitStopped` continues waiting for that same live process to set `stopped`. Consequently the daemon never reaches the in-process fallback or starts another gate in the worktree.
findings.suggestion: Track executor heartbeat freshness and provide a bounded, confirmed process-stop or recovery path before falling back.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor becomes stuck while running a gate but remains alive. Its lease expires, and the daemon waits indefinitely in `waitStopped`.

verification.trigger: An executor stalls while owning a job, remains alive, and stops renewing. Lease expiry fails the job, but stopped remains 0; fallback waits indefinitely unless externally aborted or the executor exits.

findings.title: Confinement failures are converted into a local retry
findings.detail: The executor catches every error from `executeGate`, including `ConfinementError`, and marks the job failed. The daemon treats every failed in-place job as eligible for local fallback in `lan.ts`. A confinement inspection failure can therefore be replaced by a passing second execution, hiding the failed security check and allowing the gate to pass.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the failure classification across the job boundary and propagate confinement failures without retrying them as local gates.
findings.failure_scenario: The executor cannot verify its Seatbelt confinement, but the daemon's subsequent local confinement check succeeds; the local retry passes and the original security failure is lost.

findings.title: A live but unresponsive executor is treated as fresh indefinitely
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only PID and birth time; there is no heartbeat or freshness timestamp. Lease expiry therefore does not produce a bounded fallback or a completed cancellation.

findings.title: Executor liveness has no heartbeat freshness check

The executor table has no heartbeat timestamp, so a live but stalled executor remains available indefinitely. New jobs are sent to it until pickup timeout, and waitStopped can wait indefinitely for a stalled owner after cancellation. The tests cover a dead PID and a release mismatch but never a live executor whose heartbeat stops.

findings.title: Worktree exclusivity check races with job creation
findings.detail: The scan for existing jobs and the later enqueue are separate operations with awaits between them. Two concurrent starts for the same worktree can both observe no existing job and enqueue distinct jobs, which separate executor processes can lease simultaneously. This defeats the required one-job-per-worktree guarantee.

AND state='queued'`, without a cwd exclusion. Thus neither enqueue nor leasing closes the race.

findings.title: Restart discards running retry jobs

findings.title: Executor availability has no heartbeat freshness
findings.detail: The request requires a fresh executor heartbeat and says the sweep applies freshness timers against it. Executor records contain only process identity and release, so a live but stalled executor remains available indefinitely. After a leased job expires, `waitStopped` also waits indefinitely while that process remains alive, preventing fallback.
findings.suggestion: Track executor heartbeat freshness and provide a safe way to confirm its job processes have stopped when the executor stops responding.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor process remains alive but its event loop stops responding while a gate is running. The lease expires, yet the daemon waits indefinitely for `stopped=1` rather than completing the gate or safely failing over.

verification.trigger: An executor remains alive but stops servicing its renewal timer during a gate. Lease expiry marks the job failed, yet fallback remains blocked waiting for stopped=1.

findings.title: LAN configuration bypasses the in-place executor for local repositories
findings.detail: The request says that when the executor is enabled and alive, the daemon’s local gate path creates an in-place job. With `[gates] executor = "lan"`, this branch always selects the LAN executor, whose fallback for repositories outside `workers.repos` runs directly in the daemon regardless of `[executor] enabled`.
findings.suggestion: Route the LAN executor’s local fallback through the enabled in-place executor while retaining LAN dispatch for configured repositories.
findings.failure_scenario: A coordinator uses LAN gates for one repository and enables the local executor; a different repository’s local gate still runs in the daemon and is lost on restart.

At src/gates/lan.ts:71, repositories outside the LAN list take `else if (!repos.includes(req.repo)) return local.start(req, signal)`; line 79 attaches these through `local.attach(...)`.

findings.title: Resume accepts jobs without a held lease
findings.detail: The request states, “A job is only re-attached while the executor still holds its lease.” `canResume` also accepts queued jobs and completed jobs without checking a held lease. This deviates from the requested restart boundary.

candidates.title: Rollback to an older daemon does not stop the executor
candidates.detail: The executor detects a release change only through the persistent `executor.daemonRelease` setting. A daemon from before this change never updates that setting, so after rollback it still contains the newer release SHA. The newer executor continues its running job while the older daemon resumes the run without understanding the in-place handle, allowing both releases to operate on the same worktree.
candidates.suggestion: Use a coordinator release and liveness mechanism that also detects replacement by a daemon that does not write this setting, and stop the executor's jobs before the older daemon can resume them.
candidates.failure_scenario: A new-release in-place gate is running when the daemon is rolled back to the base release. The old daemon leaves the setting unchanged and starts its own recovery or gate while the executor continues.

candidates.title: Targeted retries cannot reattach after restart
candidates.detail: The resume predicate accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A running `regression-retry-targeted` job therefore gets cancelled on restart even when its stage, round, SHA, environment, release, and lease still match. The stage repeats work instead of attaching to the retry, contrary to the requested coverage of targeted retries.
candidates.suggestion: Persist enough retry progress to resume the targeted retry at its recorded purpose and attach to its matching job.
candidates.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a long targeted regression retry is running. On resume, the saved handle fails the purpose check and the running job is cancelled.

candidates.title: A live but unresponsive executor can block a worktree indefinitely
candidates.detail: Executor freshness is determined solely by whether its PID and birth time still match; there is no heartbeat. If the executor is alive but no longer making progress, the sweep eventually fails its lease, but `waitStopped` continues waiting for that same live process to set `stopped`. Consequently the daemon never reaches the in-process fallback or starts another gate in the worktree.
candidates.suggestion: Track executor heartbeat freshness and provide a bounded, confirmed process-stop or recovery path before falling back.
candidates.failure_scenario: An executor becomes stuck while running a gate but remains alive. Its lease expires, and the daemon waits indefinitely in `waitStopped`.

candidates.title: Confinement failures are converted into a local retry
candidates.detail: The executor catches every error from `executeGate`, including `ConfinementError`, and marks the job failed. The daemon treats every failed in-place job as eligible for local fallback in `lan.ts`. A confinement inspection failure can therefore be replaced by a passing second execution, hiding the failed security check and allowing the gate to pass.
candidates.suggestion: Preserve the failure classification across the job boundary and propagate confinement failures without retrying them as local gates.
candidates.failure_scenario: The executor cannot verify its Seatbelt confinement, but the daemon's subsequent local confinement check succeeds; the local retry passes and the original security failure is lost.

candidates.title: A live but unresponsive executor is treated as fresh indefinitely
candidates.detail: Executor availability checks only PID and birth time; there is no heartbeat or freshness timestamp. If the executor remains alive but stops making progress, new jobs are sent to it and previously leased jobs eventually enter `waitStopped`, which continues waiting as long as that process exists. Lease expiry therefore does not produce a bounded fallback or a completed cancellation.
candidates.suggestion: Track executor freshness and provide a bounded, fail-closed recovery path for an unresponsive owner while confirming its gate processes have stopped.
candidates.failure_scenario: An executor hangs while running a gate and stops renewing its lease. The sweep marks the job failed, but `waitStopped` waits indefinitely because the executor PID still exists, so the run never falls back or finishes.

candidates.title: Targeted retry jobs cannot reattach after restart
candidates.detail: The resume whitelist excludes targeted and other retry purposes. When a daemon restarts during a targeted retry, the resumed stage rejects the recorded handle and cancels the surviving job instead of attaching to it. This leaves the requested restart protection incomplete for a gate purpose explicitly named in the request.
candidates.suggestion: Persist enough retry-stage state to resume the matching retry job and attach to it after restart.
candidates.failure_scenario: A long `regression-retry-targeted` job is running when the daemon restarts; the resumed gate stage cancels that job and reruns earlier gate work rather than receiving its result.

candidates.title: Targeted retry jobs cannot reattach after a restart
candidates.detail: Resume is restricted to baseline, initial and rebase purposes. Targeted retries use baseline-retry-targeted or regression-retry-targeted, so a restart rejects their matching durable handle, cancels the running job and starts the stage over. The new restart tests cover only baseline, initial and rebase, leaving this requested behavior untested.
candidates.suggestion: Persist enough retry context to resume the matching targeted job, and add a restart test that verifies the same job completes and its command runs once.
candidates.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an executor is running a regression-retry-targeted check at the same SHA; the resumed stage cancels that job instead of attaching to it.

candidates.title: Executor liveness has no heartbeat freshness check
candidates.detail: Executor availability is determined only by whether the recorded PID and birth time still match. The executor table has no heartbeat timestamp, so a live but stalled executor remains available indefinitely. New jobs are sent to it until pickup timeout, and waitStopped can wait indefinitely for a stalled owner after cancellation. The tests cover a dead PID and a release mismatch but never a live executor whose heartbeat stops.
candidates.suggestion: Track and check executor heartbeat freshness, and test a live but unresponsive executor for both fallback and cancellation behavior.
candidates.failure_scenario: An executor process remains alive but its event loop stops servicing jobs; the daemon treats it as fresh and a cancellation can remain blocked waiting for its acknowledgement.

candidates.title: Pickup timeout test does not exercise in-process fallback
candidates.detail: The pickup test stops after asserting that sweep marks an unclaimed job failed. It never attaches through the gate executor or verifies that the check subsequently runs locally and returns its result, so a regression in the failed-job fallback path would pass.
candidates.suggestion: Add a test that leaves an in-place job unclaimed, advances through pickup expiry, and asserts the local check executes and its GateRun is returned.
candidates.failure_scenario: The sweep marks the job failed, but the attach loop fails to launch or return the in-process fallback; the existing test still passes.

candidates.title: Executor tests replace the confinement they need to verify
candidates.detail: The subprocess explicitly installs a no-op confinement wrapper, and the parent uses fakeConfinement. Consequently the test can pass even if executor gates run without the daemon's required confinement. Existing output and environment assertions do not exercise this boundary.
candidates.suggestion: Add a platform-gated real confinement probe through the executor that checks both an allowed worktree operation and a denied out-of-scope write.
candidates.failure_scenario: The executor launches a gate without its required confinement; every new executor test still passes because the test fixture disables confinement.

candidates.title: Executor output is redacted with an incomplete credential registry
candidates.detail: Credential registration is process-local. The executor loads configuration, but it does not register credentials acquired by the daemon at runtime, such as its API token, GitHub token, or worker tokens. Gate output is redacted and truncated in the executor and then written to job events and results using that executor's registry. A credential known only to the daemon can therefore be persisted unredacted, and truncation can prevent the daemon from recognizing it later.
candidates.suggestion: Make the executor's redaction policy cover the daemon's dynamically registered credentials before it captures, truncates, or persists gate output.
candidates.failure_scenario: A gate prints a daemon-registered API or GitHub token that is absent from the executor's credential registry; the token appears in the stored gate event or result.

candidates.title: A live but stalled executor is treated as fresh indefinitely
candidates.detail: Executor availability checks only the PID and birth identity; there is no heartbeat or freshness timestamp. If the executor process remains alive but stops polling or renewing, the daemon continues to consider it available. For a leased job, waitStopped also waits indefinitely for that same process instead of reaching a confirmed-stop recovery path.
candidates.suggestion: Track and check executor heartbeat freshness, and provide a bounded, fail-closed recovery path for a stale owner.
candidates.failure_scenario: An executor process stalls while running a gate and remains alive. Its lease expires, but the daemon waits indefinitely for stopped to become 1 and cannot fall back or start the next gate.

candidates.title: Worktree exclusivity check races with job creation
candidates.detail: The scan for existing jobs and the later enqueue are separate operations with awaits between them. Two concurrent starts for the same worktree can both observe no existing job and enqueue distinct jobs, which separate executor processes can lease simultaneously. This defeats the required one-job-per-worktree guarantee.
candidates.suggestion: Serialize reservation and enqueue for a worktree with an atomic database constraint or transaction, retaining the reservation until process cleanup is confirmed.
candidates.failure_scenario: Two gate starts for the same cwd run concurrently while two executors are available. Both pass the empty-job scan, enqueue, and execute checks in the same worktree at once.

candidates.title: Restart discards running retry jobs
candidates.detail: The request says that a resumed stage whose handle matches its stage, round, purpose, and SHA attaches to it, and explicitly includes the targeted retry. This allowlist rejects timeout and regression retry purposes even when all of those fields match. The stage’s initial resume check also cancels a recorded retry before it can be attached.
candidates.suggestion: Persist enough retry-stage state to resume the recorded retry, and validate its matching handle without restricting resumption to the first execution.
candidates.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an executor runs `regression-retry-targeted`; the resumed stage cancels that job and repeats earlier gates instead of receiving the retry result.

candidates.title: Executor availability has no heartbeat freshness
candidates.detail: The request requires a fresh executor heartbeat and says the sweep applies freshness timers against it. Executor records contain only process identity and release, so a live but stalled executor remains available indefinitely. After a leased job expires, `waitStopped` also waits indefinitely while that process remains alive, preventing fallback.
candidates.suggestion: Track executor heartbeat freshness and provide a safe way to confirm its job processes have stopped when the executor stops responding.
candidates.failure_scenario: An executor process remains alive but its event loop stops responding while a gate is running. The lease expires, yet the daemon waits indefinitely for `stopped=1` rather than completing the gate or safely failing over.

candidates.title: LAN configuration bypasses the in-place executor for local repositories
candidates.detail: The request says that when the executor is enabled and alive, the daemon’s local gate path creates an in-place job. With `[gates] executor = "lan"`, this branch always selects the LAN executor, whose fallback for repositories outside `workers.repos` runs directly in the daemon regardless of `[executor] enabled`.
candidates.suggestion: Route the LAN executor’s local fallback through the enabled in-place executor while retaining LAN dispatch for configured repositories.
candidates.failure_scenario: A coordinator uses LAN gates for one repository and enables the local executor; a different repository’s local gate still runs in the daemon and is lost on restart.

candidates.title: Resume accepts jobs without a held lease
candidates.detail: The request states, “A job is only re-attached while the executor still holds its lease.” `canResume` also accepts queued jobs and completed jobs without checking a held lease. This deviates from the requested restart boundary.
candidates.suggestion: Require a current executor-held lease for reattachment, or explicitly define and implement a separate completed-result recovery rule.
candidates.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after saving a handle while the job is still queued; the resumed stage reattaches to that unleased job instead of starting fresh.
